title: P1 resilience: the reqwest whole-request 180s deadline kills healthy SSE streams
description:
src/core/executor/client_pool.rs:191 applies .timeout(timeout.stream), and reqwest's timeout() runs from request start until the response BODY finishes — not until headers. send_one (default.rs:2298) returns Ok at response headers, so a healthy long SSE stream on the reqwest path is killed at 180s regardless of the stall watchdog.

This is why the timeout work could NOT be one bead: the two deadlines sit on OPPOSITE sides of the send() boundary. Splitting them is the point. use_hyper_transport (default.rs:2409) chooses the path, and build_hyper_client (:209-230) has NO total timeout — so the fix is either to move the reqwest deadline to a header-only timeout, or to route long streams onto the hyper client, or to drop the total cap and rely on the stall watchdog. State which, and why.

DEPENDS ON nothing; the stall-watchdog bead (separate) is independent of this one and must not be merged back.

VERIFY: pin the transport in the test. A stream that emits a chunk every 30s for 10 minutes must NOT be cut off; a stream that emits nothing must still terminate via the watchdog, not via this deadline.
close_reason: reqwest .timeout() (whole-lifecycle) replaced with .read_timeout() (per-read) so long streams survive and the watchdog decides. Commits 0fd30631, 7c5efe7c.

title: P0: opening the basic chat page can erase stored chat history
description:
Found by peer review 2026-09-25. DEFERRED by user decision. Filed on its own
because it is the highest-severity item from that sweep and is NOT the same
class as the config-write bugs.

BasicChatPageClient.tsx:270 and :441 use `safeParse`, which swallows a parse
failure into `[]`. The persist effect then writes `JSON.stringify([])` — on
MOUNT. Opening the page therefore erases the user's chat history with no click,
no confirmation, and no error.

VERIFY: a stored history that fails to parse is surfaced as an error and left
untouched; the persist effect does not run against a failed read.
close_reason: Fixed. safeParse turned a present-but-unreadable stored value into an empty list, which is indistinguishable from 'no history' to every consumer; the persist effect, gated only on isHydrated (set in the loader's finally), then wrote that empty list back. Opening the page destroyed the history with no click and no error. The loader now separates absent from unreadable: absent still hydrates empty, unreadable surfaces a message and clears a new storageWritable flag that makes the persist effect return early, leaving the stored bytes recoverable. The message uses its own state because loadData resets loadError on every run and would wipe it a tick after mount. safeParse had no other caller and is removed. Verified: 216 pages build.

title: P0 streaming: SSE frame-boundary de-framing (multi-frame and split reads)
description:
One transport chunk is treated as exactly one logical SSE event. A chunk carrying several frames, or a frame split across reads, is mishandled. 9router buffers per line (.tmp/9router/open-sse/utils/stream.js:110-119). Evidence in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'frame-boundary' / 'P11-001').

This is the FOUNDATION the other streaming beads build on: a named-event Anthropic frame is 'event: X\ndata: {...}', and usage extraction cannot see the data line until the chunk is de-framed. The usage-merge bead (kh7f) is CLOSED — shipped in 7c553c85/38b5fe2a — but this framing work is still live: strip_sse_data_prefix remains per-chunk and stateless, so a data: line split across two reads is never reassembled..

SCOPE: a stateful line/frame buffer in front of translate_response, plus a flush_stream EOF hook so a trailing frame with no newline is still emitted. The buffer must ensure a frame straddling two reads is acted on exactly ONCE — a naive re-scan double-counts it.

VERIFY: feed a stream where one TCP read carries two frames, and another where a single frame straddles two reads. Both must produce byte-identical output to the equivalent single-read stream. Assert a frame containing '{' inside a string value is not split.
close_reason: Byte-buffered SSE framing on BOTH arms (Hyper was the default arm and was missed first time). Commits 764469cd, db47e5f0; regression fixes 1c3d806f, e166b0bd. 9 router rounds, 2 P0 caught in review.

title: P0: kimi-coding is missing from PROVIDER_CONFIGS -> HTTP 500 on every request
description:
P0 BLOCKER. Confirmed by the reviewer by parsing PROVIDER_CONFIGS directly: 103 entries. `kimi` is PRESENT. `agentrouter`, `glm`, `minimax`, `minimax-cn`, `claude`, `anthropic`, `openai` are all PRESENT. `kimi-coding` is MISSING.

THE DEFECT: `kimi-coding` is a first-class provider everywhere EXCEPT the routing table.
  - src/oauth/providers.rs:205 defines an OAuth provider whose id is `kimi-coding`.
  - src/oauth/token_refresh.rs:1135 handles `"kimi" | "kimi-coding"` in the device-code flow.
  - src/oauth/mod.rs:5 lists kimi-coding as a device-code provider.
  - src/core/executor/default.rs PROVIDER_CONFIGS has no `kimi-coding` key.

When a connection is configured through the kimi-coding OAuth path (with no provider_node), dispatch resolves provider = "kimi-coding", then `DefaultExecutor::new` does `PROVIDER_CONFIGS.get(provider)` -> None -> `ExecutorError::UnsupportedProvider` -> HTTP 500 on every request. The user configured the provider successfully via OAuth and then every single call fails with an opaque 500.

STEP 1 — CONFIRM REACHABILITY before writing the fix: verify that a kimi-coding connection created through the OAuth path reaches `DefaultExecutor::new` with no provider_node attached. If some other layer maps it to the existing `kimi` entry first, that is a different (also worth fixing) bug — capture which, in the bead comment.

THE FIX: add the `kimi-coding` entry to PROVIDER_CONFIGS, modelled on the existing `kimi` entry (same base URL and Claude-compatible shape the OAuth flow actually returns). Check the existing `kimi` entry first and mirror it rather than inventing a new shape.

VERIFICATION:
- A test asserting every id reachable from the OAuth provider registry and from the device-code provider list has a PROVIDER_CONFIGS entry. Make it data-driven over the registry so a future provider cannot be added without a routing entry.
- A test that constructing the executor for `kimi-coding` succeeds.
- Run the kiro/kiro-coding-style parity tests to confirm the analogous provider is not also missing.
close_reason: kimi-coding PROVIDER_CONFIGS entry + registry-coverage test; commit 8ebcc216

title: 1.4 - Response Translation & SSE Streaming
description:
Response Translation & SSE Streaming

## Scope
Translate upstream response chunks to client format. SSE transform stream with usage extraction.

## Subtasks
1. SSE event parser: parse lines, reconstruct JSON chunks, handle buffer boundaries
2. Response translator dispatch: target->source format conversion (reverse of request)
3. SINGLE [DONE] sentinel — 9router bug: DOUBLE [DONE] in translate AND passthrough modes
4. Token usage extraction from ALL formats with fallback estimation
5. Streaming handler: pipe provider Response through SSE transform to client
6. Non-streaming handler: SSE-to-JSON when provider forces streaming
7. Buffer size limit (prevent OOM from pathological provider chunks)
8. Cache-control-aware usage: buffer 2000 tokens to prevent context window errors

## CRITICAL 9router Fixes
- DOUBLE [DONE] sentinel: transform() emits one, flush() emits another. Fix: single emit with completion flag.
- toolArgBuffers Map not initialized: tool call arguments can vanish during streaming. Fix: pre-initialize.
- Error swallowing in flush(): all errors caught and logged but not propagated. Fix: controller.error() on failure.
- usage filter uses sourceFormat instead of post-translation format: non-OpenAI clients get empty usage. Fix: filter after translation.
- Gemini thoughtsTokenCount into prompt_tokens: misclassifies thinking as input. Fix: prepend to completion_tokens.

## Files
- src/stream/sse.rs — SSE line parser + serializer
- src/stream/transform.rs — Transform stream implementation
- src/stream/handler.rs — Streaming handler
- src/stream/json_handler.rs — SSE-to-JSON for non-streaming path

title: P0: disabled custom models never leave the available list (breaks Providers page / ModelSelectModal mirror rule)
description:
P0. This is the AGENTS.md core-surface rule: the Providers page (surface #1) and ModelSelectModal (surface #4) must mirror each other EXACTLY. Today they do not, and the violation is silent.

THE DEFECT: disabled custom models are never filtered out of the available list.
  web/src/shared/models/availableModels.ts:165  stamps `disabled: disabledSet.has(r.id)` on every custom row
  web/src/shared/models/availableModels.ts:176  enabledRows = [...customRows, ...enabledCoreRows]   <-- customRows is NOT filtered

The `disabled` flag on a custom row is WRITE-ONLY: there is no consumer of it anywhere in web/src. Consequences, all four at once:
 - web/src/components/providers/ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:1149-1150 renders am.customRows, so the model stays visible on the Providers page.
 - web/src/shared/components/ModelSelectModal.tsx:342 and :431 map built.enabledRows, so it stays selectable in the opencode picker. This is the mirror-rule break.
 - ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:1156 passes NO onDisable for custom rows, and web/src/shared/components/ModelRow.tsx:113 gates the block button on `{!isCustom && onDisable}` — a custom row is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of being disabled individually.
 - The "Disabled models" restore section (:1285) and the "Active All" gate (:1781) both read am.disabledCoreRows only, so a lone disabled custom model has no escape hatch.

The backend accepts the write (src/server/api/models_disabled.rs:145-154 takes arbitrary ids with no catalog validation), so the POST succeeds and the state persists while the UI ignores it.

REPRO: Providers -> any provider -> Add Model `my-tuned-model` -> Disable All -> toast says "Disabled N model(s)"; reload: the row is still there, still selectable in the opencode picker, no disable button, no restore entry.

THE FIX:
 - Split custom rows the same way core rows are split:
     enabledRows  = [...customRows.filter(r => !r.disabled), ...enabledCoreRows]
     disabledRows = [...customRows.filter(r =>  r.disabled), ...disabledCoreRows]
 - Pass onDisable on the custom row and relax ModelRow.tsx:113 so the block button renders whenever onDisable exists.
 - Point the restore section and the "Active All" gate at the combined disabled set.
 - Then audit ModelSelectModal for the OTHER mirror divergences the same review surfaced, all in this same shared-data path:
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:95 defaults modelAliases = {} and 3 of 16 tool pickers never pass the prop (ClineToolCard.tsx:461-467, DefaultToolCard.tsx:347-354, KiloToolCard.tsx:451-457). For compatible providers modelAliases is the ONLY source of real models, so an empty prop degrades to a literal placeholder. Fix by fetching /api/models/alias inside the modal on isOpen (pattern already at :140-221) and letting the prop override.
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:454 groupedModels memo omits catalog readiness, unlike the provider page (availableModels.ts:395-401). Violates the mirror rule; opens showing zero models with no recovery.
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:386-419 the kindFilter branch bypasses buildAvailableModels entirely and its custom-row map never sets `type`, so filterByKind (:271-274) discards EVERY custom typed model.
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:440-442 injects a synthetic {value: alias} row when a provider has no models, so a fully-disabled provider still offers a bare alias that resolves to the wrong provider (core/model/mod.rs:285-345). Guard on built.allRows.length === 0.
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:247-258 the freeOnly fetch has no localStorage fallback while availableModels.ts:248-269 does, and saveFreeOnly writes localStorage FIRST (:271-286) — one failed PUT desynchronizes the two surfaces permanently on a healthy backend. Export and call loadFreeOnly.
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:484-492 search matches m.name/m.id but never m.value or group.alias, so typing a short alias filters the group out entirely (39 of 105 providers have an alias that is not a substring of the display name).
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:494-499 a provider-name-only match emits a group with models: [], rendering a bare header with (0) and suppressing the "No models found" fallback. Reproduced against real data: "kilo" -> Kilo Code (0). Change the condition to matchedModels.length > 0.
     * ModelSelectModal.tsx:63 NO_AUTH_PROVIDER_IDS includes hidden:true providers (devin-cli, mimo-free — providers.ts:20-21); the modal has no hidden check, so phantom groups render.

VERIFICATION (must go red first):
 - Disable a custom model, then assert it disappears from the Providers page list, moves to the "Disabled (N)" section, AND disappears from the ModelSelectModal — all three, in one test, because the mirror rule is the whole point.
 - Assert the modal and the provider page report the same enabled set for the same provider (a direct mirror assertion is more durable than three separate assertions).

REMEMBER: cd web && pnpm build before you consider the change visible.
close_reason: custom rows split by disabled state; commit e5db61ab

title: per-provider executor streaming (cursor/zed/codex/qoder)
description:
PART OF A SPLIT, re-filed by polish round 3 — the original area clustering mis-binned findings by subsystem. CHECK THE WORKING TREE FIRST: several predate fixes that have since landed, and some were duplicates of a sibling bead's item, now removed.

COMPLETION RULE: this is a WORK LIST. Every finding is confirmed and in scope. If you believe one is unreachable, PROVE it by naming the guard and delete the finding. 'Low value' is not a reason.

   GAP: OpenProxy re-mints a Zed LLM token on every request and has no expiry-triggered refresh retry, whereas 9router caches the token for 50 minutes and force-refreshes once on a 401 or expired/outdated-token signal.
8. [P1] Zed live model catalog resolution (open-sse/shared/zedAuth.js + src/app/api/v1/models/route.js → src/core/executor/zed.rs)
   GAP: OpenProxy never performs the live Zed model-catalog fetch that 9router uses for both per-request model→provider resolution and `GET /v1/models` advertising, so it always relies on the name-substring heuristic and can never list Zed's hosted

   GAP: No 401 or `x-zed-expired-token`/`x-zed-outdated-token` detection and no token-refresh retry on the Zed completion path.

   GAP: OpenProxy omits the `Accept`, `User-Agent` and `x-zed-version` headers that 9router sends on the Zed completions request, while still assuming an NDJSON response body.

   GAP: The boolean capability headers use the string `"1"` on the OpenProxy side and the string `"true"` on the 9router side.

   GAP: Three request headers present on every 9router Zed call are absent: the NDJSON `Accept`, the `User-Agent`, and `x-zed-version`.

   GAP: The default-instructions trigger tests emptiness in 9Router but only raw non-emptiness in OpenProxy, so a whitespace-only `instructions` value suppresses the default Codex agent prompt in OpenProxy while 9Router still injects it.
14. [P2] open-sse/executors/codex.js:428 vs src/core/executor/codex.rs:405-409
   GAP: The emptiness test is `trim() === \"\"` in 9Router but `is_empty()` (no trim) in OpenProxy, so whitespace-only `instructions` is replaced by the full Codex default upstream and preserved downstream.

   GAP: OpenProxy never recurses into an array-valued `properties` node, so a `\p{...}` pattern nested there is never stripped and reaches Codex, whereas 9Router's fall-through recursion strips it.
16. [P3] open-sse/config/codexInstructions.js:90,109,115,116 vs src/core/executor/codex.rs:368
   GAP: OpenProxy holds two divergent copies of the same default-instructions constant: the one that is actually sent (ASCII hyphens) differs from 9Router in 4 characters, while the copy that is byte-identical to 9Router is never read.

   GAP: The inlined default Codex instructions differ from 9Router's at four characters: OpenProxy uses ASCII hyphens where 9Router uses U+2011 non-breaking hyphens, even though an unused data file in the same repo already holds the byte-exact stri
18. [P1] open-sse/shared/qoder/cosy.js:147-148 vs src/core/executor/qoder.rs:1503-1511
   GAP: The COSY signature is computed over a lossy UTF-8 rendering of the body instead of the body's actual bytes.
19. [P3] Qoder prompt-size estimate feeding context-tier selection (open-sse/shared/qoder/contextTier.js → src/core/executor/qoder.rs)
   GAP: OpenProxy counts Unicode scalar values where 9router counts UTF-16 code units, underestimating the Qoder prompt size for content containing astral-plane characters.
20. [P3] open-sse/shared/qoder/attachments.js:275-292 vs src/core/executor/qoder.rs:1249-1284,993-998
   GAP: In the over-budget pass OpenProxy keeps every data-URI at or below 512 KB, whereas 9router strips them all.

title: P0 streaming: port 9router's passthrough transform set
description:
OpenProxy's SSE passthrough is a near-raw byte copy and performs NONE of 9router's passthrough transforms (.tmp/9router/open-sse/utils/stream.js:135-241 and :385-409): fixInvalidId, object/created injection when choices is present, Azure field deletion, empty-tool_calls deletion, hasValuableContent skip, usage merge, and finish-chunk usage attachment; plus an EOF 'data: [DONE]\n\n' unless the provider is antigravity/gemini/vertex.

This is a separate concern from framing and from the guard: it is what a NORMAL passthrough stream must contain, as opposed to how chunks are split or how non-SSE is rejected.

9router's estimated-usage injection onto the finish chunk (stream.js:204-210) is the piece OpenProxy has never had at all. Note there is no usage estimator anywhere in the Rust usage path — UsageTracker::track_request coerces None to 0, and there is no estimate function in the Rust usage path. If the finish-chunk estimator is wanted, it is added HERE.

DEPENDS ON: the framing split, since these transforms operate per logical frame. Evidence in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'passthrough').

VERIFY: a passthrough stream asserts each transform fires on its own input (invalid id fixed, object/created injected, Azure fields removed, empty tool_calls dropped, EOF [DONE] present for OpenAI-shaped and ABSENT for antigravity/gemini/vertex), and a stream with no usage frame still gets a finish-chunk estimate if the estimator is ported.
close_reason: 9router passthrough transform set: fixInvalidId, object/created injection, Azure field deletion, empty tool_calls removal, EOF DONE sentinel. Commit 3ac819b3.

title: parity: map the 12 remaining 9router aliases whose target has no PROVIDER_CONFIGS entry
description:
The alias-parity bead added 38 mappings whose targets are real PROVIDER_CONFIGS keys. Twelve were deliberately skipped because their target is dispatched by its own executor rather than through PROVIDER_CONFIGS: brave-search, commandcode, devin-cli, fish-audio, grok-cli (gb / gcli / grok-build), trae (marscode / tr), aws-polly, qoder (qd), stability-ai, venice.

CORRECTION (bead review): the original version of this bead claimed get_model_info() looks up PROVIDER_CONFIGS, and that remapping an alias therefore changes routing. THAT PREMISE WAS FALSE. get_model_info (src/core/model/mod.rs:259-333) does not reference PROVIDER_CONFIGS at all; it resolves via provider_nodes, then db.combos, then db.model_aliases, then infer_provider_from_model_name. Remapping an alias only changes the provider string handed to the chat.rs dispatch match.

So the task is to trace what the dispatch match actually does with each provider string, which is a much smaller and more tractable question:

TASK, per alias:
  1. Confirm with the CURRENT code that the unmapped alias reaches a working executor. chat.rs matches `grok-cli|gcli|gb|grok-build` on the GrokCli arm, so those four already route. Check whether `qd`, `tr`, `marscode`, `cmd`-style short forms and the rest are likewise matched by name at their dispatch arms.

title: P0 streaming: SSE frame-boundary correctness and the non-SSE guard
description:
Three related P0s in the SSE path, same code, fix together. Full evidence in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'SSE').

1. One transport chunk is treated as exactly one logical SSE event. A chunk
   carrying several frames, or a frame split across reads, is mishandled.
   9router buffers per line (open-sse/utils/stream.js:110-119).
2. The non-SSE guard is a 3-type deny-list returning a hardcoded 502, where
   9router pipes the body. Verified consequence: a 2xx application/json from a
   provider that ignored stream:true becomes a 502, and 502 is RETRYABLE for
   multi-provider clients, so one flaky provider triggers a retry storm. An
   unlisted non-SSE type is piped into the SSE transform, yielding garbage
   frames with no terminal [DONE] — the hang the guard exists to prevent. Raw
   upstream HTML is echoed into error.message, which is the XSS surface
   9router's own comment says the title-clamp exists to block.
3. The passthrough is a near-raw byte copy and performs none of 9router's
   passthrough transforms (fixInvalidId, object/created injection, Azure field
   deletion, empty tool_calls deletion, usage merge, finish-chunk usage
   attachment, and an EOF data: [DONE] unless the provider is
   antigravity/gemini/vertex).

FIX: line-buffered framing with a state machine so a frame split across reads is
acted on once; align the non-SSE guard with 9router's rule and never echo raw
upstream bytes into an error message; implement the passthrough transform set
above.

VERIFY: feed a stream where one TCP read carries two frames and another where a
frame straddles two reads — both must produce identical output. Assert the EOF
[DONE] is emitted for OpenAI-shaped providers and NOT for antigravity/gemini/
vertex. Assert a 200-with-JSON-body yields a well-formed client response, not a
502 and not raw HTML.
close_reason: Split by polish round 1 — the three findings are different code regions, not 'the same code'. Superseded by openproxy-0ph4 (framing), openproxy-n12c (non-SSE guard), openproxy-3bt9 (passthrough transforms). Content preserved across the three.

title: P0: combo --strategy is written into Combo.kind, hiding the combo and no-oping the strategy
description:
P0. Core surface #3 (Combos page). Confirmed by two independent verification lenses.

THE DEFECT: `openproxy combo create --strategy X` writes X into `Combo.kind`.
  src/cli/combo.rs:190  kind: normalize_strategy(&strategy)
  src/cli/combo.rs:224  combo.kind = normalize_strategy(s)
  src/cli/combo.rs:405-407 (apply path), default "fallback" at :36

`kind` means media modality (llm / tts / image), NOT dispatch strategy. Three consequences, all silent:
 (a) web/src/components/CombosPageClient.tsx:113 filters `!c.kind || c.kind === "llm"`, so a combo with kind="round-robin" is INVISIBLE on the Combos page — the user creates a combo and it does not appear.
 (b) src/server/api/v1_models.rs:408-411 `combo_matches_kinds` drops it from GET /v1/models — the combo is not listed.
 (c) src/core/combo/mod.rs:170-184 `strategy_for_combo` reads settings.combo_strategies[name] -> combo.extra["strategy"] -> global default. It NEVER reads `kind`. So the requested strategy is a silent no-op and the combo runs plain fallback.

Every CLI-created combo is affected, because `--strategy` defaults to "fallback" and normalize_strategy returns Some("fallback").

REPRO: openproxy combo create --name mymix --models openai/gpt-4o,anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 --strategy round-robin  =>  /api/combos shows "kind":"round-robin"; absent from /v1/models and from the Combos page; requests to mymix run plain fallback.

THE FIX:
 1. In run_create / run_edit / run_apply write the strategy to combo.extra["strategy"] (or settings.combo_strategies[name]) and leave `kind` for modality only.
 2. Add a one-time SQLite patch (src/db/sqlite/patch.rs) rewriting combos.kind -> NULL where the value is one of the strategy names {fallback, round-robin, sticky-round-robin, fusion, auto-combo, hedging, shadow, cheapest, fastest, quality}. Existing users have this corruption in their DB right now.
 3. Related contract defect, same fix: src/cli/schema.rs:167 advertises top-level `strategy` and `:170` `isActive` on the combo schema, but CreateComboRequest (src/server/api/mod.rs:1451) has neither field and no #[serde(flatten)], so serde silently drops them; UpdateComboRequest (src/server/api/admin_items.rs:429) has no `extra` at all. The schema must reflect what the write path honours. The schema enum also omits cheapest/fastest/quality which parse_combo_strategy supports and the Combos page offers, and includes sticky-round-robin which has NO arm in parse_combo_strategy (silently falls back) — either implement the arm or remove it from the frozen enum. NOTE: the openproxy.v1.* schema namespace is frozen additive-only; removing a member from an enum is a breaking change, so implement the arm rather than deleting the value, and record the decision in the bead comment.

VERIFICATION:
 - CLI create/edit/apply with each strategy: assert combos.kind is NULL/absent and the strategy is honored at dispatch.
 - A migration test that a pre-existing row with kind="round-robin" is patched to NULL.
 - A schema round-trip test: `openproxy schema example combo` -> POST it -> the response carries the same strategy back (today it is silently dropped).
close_reason: strategy lands in extra not kind + repair wired into apply_pending_migrations; commits ba2e8c7d, c9703ac3

title: P0: opencode.jsonc parsed as strict JSON can wipe the user's whole config
description:
P0 BLOCKER — DATA LOSS. Reported by the audit; confirm it by reading src/server/api/cli_tools.rs around line 1429 before fixing, because the severity here is "silently destroys the user's configuration".

THE DEFECT: `opencode.jsonc` is a JSONC file (JSON with comments) — that is the entire point of the extension, and users put comments in it. If the opencode config writer parses it with a strict JSON parser, any comment anywhere in the file makes the parse fail. If the failure path then proceeds to write a freshly-built config, the user's entire opencode configuration — model, MCP server entries, permissions, API keys — is overwritten and the comments are gone. OpenProxy is supposed to be the thing that WIRES UP opencode, not the thing that destroys its config.

THE FIX, in order of preference:
1. parse opencode.jsonc with a real JSONC parser (strip // and /* */ comments and trailing commas before strict parse), and on parse failure RETURN AN ERROR and leave the file untouched. Never fall through to "write default config" when the existing file was present but unreadable.
2. If a JSONC dependency is not wanted, at minimum: refuse to write when the existing file fails to parse, and tell the user exactly which file and which line. Preserving the user's file beats generating a valid one.

VERIFICATION (must go red first):
- A test that writes an opencode.jsonc containing a `//` comment and a real config, triggers the Apply path, and asserts (a) the resulting file still parses, (b) the comment survives, (c) no pre-existing key was dropped.
- A test that an unparseable opencode.json is NOT overwritten and returns a clear error.
close_reason: opencode.jsonc parsed as JSONC + fail-closed; commit 1e28d8f4

title: P0: Combo.extra is never persisted (lost on restart) and combo disable writes a key nobody reads
description:
P0 — DATA PERSISTENCE. Core surface #3. Confirmed by two verification lenses.

THE DEFECT, two layers:

(1) `combo disable` writes a key nobody reads. src/cli/combo.rs:279 sets combo.extra["isActive"] and prints success. But `Combo` (src/types/mod.rs:394-415) has no `is_active` field, and neither get_combo_models_from_data (src/core/combo/mod.rs:723-732) nor get_model_info (src/core/model/mod.rs:267) consults `extra`. The combo keeps serving. The CLI reports success for a no-op.

(2) WORSE — `extra` is not persisted at all. src/db/sqlite/repo/combo_repo.rs:35 writes `extra` into the data column, but row_to_combo binds it to `let _data` and rebuilds the struct with `..Default::default()` (combo_repo.rs:59, 72) — the value is read and thrown away. src/db/sqlite/export.rs:171-186 selects that column and never reads index 4. src/db/sqlite/import.rs:170 writes a literal "{}". Since Db::load_from rebuilds from export_all (src/db/mod.rs:145-152) and spawn_watcher is a no-op (src/db/watcher.rs:13-15), **`extra` is lost on every restart**. So strategy, isActive, fusionConfig and judgeModel all vanish on restart.

REPRO: openproxy combo disable mymix -> exit 0, envelope openproxy.v1.combo.disable; POST /v1/chat/completions {"model":"mymix"} still 200s through the combo; after a restart even the isActive:false echo is gone.

THE FIX:
 - Parse `extra` in row_to_combo and emit it from export_all / import. This is the durable root fix.
 - Add a real `is_active: Option<bool>` to `Combo` and honour it in get_combo_models_from_data, in list_models, and in the Combos page filter.

VERIFICATION:
 - Create a combo carrying `extra`, restart the process (or reload from a fresh Db::load_from on the same path), assert `extra` survives byte-identical.
 - `combo disable` -> the combo is no longer dispatched, and survives a restart.
 - Regression: an existing combo with empty extra still loads.
close_reason: Combo.extra persisted + is_active honored; commits bf1d3c47, c9703ac3

title: Release readiness: verified defect remediation
description:

SHARED RULES FOR EVERY BEAD:

- Do not weaken the `openproxy.v1.*` robot schema: it is a FROZEN additive-only contract. New fields only, never renames or removals.
- No secrets in the tree, robot output, or logs.

title: P1: MCP transport has no auth; unauthenticated read-only tool enumeration
description:
P1. SECURITY. The audit reported this as a blocker ("unauthenticated MCP exposes unredacted provider credentials"). The reviewer ran a LIVE PoC and DOWNGRADED it. Read this before you touch the code — do not build a fix for the claim as originally stated.

WHAT THE REVIEWER ACTUALLY PROVED (live server on a temp DATA_DIR, curl):
 - `POST /api/mcp` with tools/call key_create and NO credentials -> {"error":"Tool 'key_create' requires authentication. Pass a valid API key via the '_api_key' argument."}
 - with a bogus _api_key -> {"error":"Invalid or inactive API key"}
 - tools/list with no auth -> 17 tool NAMES returned (information disclosure)
 - key_list with no auth -> metadata only: id, name, is_active, created_at. NO plaintext key.
 - settings_get with no auth -> a 73-line settings blob; a scan for key|token|secret|password|credential|authorization matched only authMode and hasPassword. No secrets.
 - /api/mcp-server/sse with no auth -> opens and emits a session endpoint frame.

SO: the credential-theft takeover is REFUTED. What is real:
 (1) The MCP transport has NO authentication of its own. src/server/api/mcp_server.rs routes() is merged into the `remaining` router in src/server/api/mod.rs (~:408), which has no route_layer (contrast the `admin` router at :385 using guard::require_admin). The handlers `sse_handler` and `stateless_mcp_handler` take no HeaderMap and call no require_* helper. Authentication is pushed down into individual tool handlers via the `_api_key` argument.
 (2) Consequences: unauthenticated read-only tools are callable — tool inventory, API-key inventory, settings, usage status, model list, health. Any local process (or anything that can reach the port when the user binds 0.0.0.0) can enumerate that.
 (3) Design fragility: secrets travel as a JSON-RPC tool ARGUMENT rather than through transport auth. Arguments are the part most likely to end up in access logs, traces, or crash dumps. This is the shape that turns a future tool bug into a credential leak.

THE FIX (in this order of preference):
 (a) Add transport-level auth to mcp_server::routes(): either move it into the `admin` router, or add its own route_layer requiring the dashboard session / management API key, matching how every other admin surface is protected. Keep the per-tool `_api_key` check as defence in depth — do not remove it.
 (b) If a transport guard would break local MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline) that legitimately call this endpoint, then instead: (i) gate the read-only tools behind the same check the mutating ones already use, and (ii) make the SSE stream authenticate before emitting the session endpoint frame. Document which choice you made and why.

VERIFICATION:
 - A test that an unauthenticated POST /api/mcp cannot invoke ANY tool (including the read-only ones) once you implement (a) — or, if you choose (b), that the read-only tools reject.
 - A test that an authorized client still works end to end, so you have not simply broken MCP for every user.
 - Keep a regression test that a bogus _api_key is still rejected at the tool layer.

title: 2.3 - Account Fallback & Model-Level Locking
description:
Account Fallback & Model-Level Locking

## Scope
Model-level error handling with exponential backoff. Error classification: should_fallback vs non-recoverable. Rate limit cascade prevention.

## Subtasks
1. Model-level locking: modelLock_{model} timestamps per connection
2. Account-level lock fallback: modelLock___all when no specific model
3. Exponential backoff cooldown with CORRECT doubling (9router: off-by-one, level 0 and 1 both 2s)
4. Clear lock on successful request + lazy cleanup of expired locks
5. Error classification: should_fallback vs non-recoverable (400/404 should NOT fallback)
6. 429 TRANSIENT COOLDOWN before next combo model (9router: no delay = cascade)
7. Error text matching with ERROR_RULES config (substring-based, top-to-bottom priority)

## CRITICAL 9router Fixes
- shouldFallback ALWAYS true: default branch returns shouldFallback=true for ALL unmatched errors. Fix: 400/404/500 return false.
- Dead rateLimitedUntil field: active locking writes modelLock_*, not rateLimitedUntil. Fix: use only modelLock_* fields.
- Backoff off-by-one: getQuotaCooldown(max(0, level-1)). Fix: base * 2^level with no offset.
- 429 cascade with NO delay between combo models. Fix: apply cooldownMs before next model.
- filterAvailableAccounts checks rateLimitedUntil which is never written. Fix: use isModelLockActive.

## Files
- src/fallback/error.rs — ErrorRule matching, should_fallback logic
- src/fallback/backoff.rs — Exponential backoff calculation
- src/fallback/lock.rs — ModelLock read/write
- src/fallback/clear.rs — ClearAccountError + lazy cleanup

## Tests
- 429 triggers fallback with cooldown
- 400 (Bad Request) does NOT fallback
- Model lock prevents selection on next request
- Clear on success removes model lock
- Expired locks auto-cleaned
- Rate limit cascade prevented with delay

description:
# Epic: 9router → OpenProxy Logic Parity Hardening

## Background
OpenProxy (Rust 0.1.2) ports 9router (JS 0.5.30, open-sse). Evidence audit against `/tmp/9router` found modules that exist but are unwired, wrong protocol surfaces, and pipeline-order mismatches. Small divergences break Claude Code, Kiro, Codex, fusion combos, DeepSeek TUI, GitHub Codex models.

Reference roots (read-only; do NOT copy JS bugs blindly):
- JS core: `/tmp/9router/open-sse/` — handlers, executors, translator, services, config
- JS entry: `/tmp/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js`
- Rust hot path: `src/server/api/chat.rs`
- Rust core: `src/core/{chat,combo,executor,translator,account_fallback,config}/`
- OAuth: `src/oauth/`

## Why this epic exists (project goals)
OpenProxy’s purpose (AGENTS.md): replace 9router with a faster, safer Rust router **without losing working client/provider behavior**. Type safety and encryption are wins only if drop-in routing still works. This epic is the bridge from “code exists” to “behavior matches.”

## Overarching goals
1. Behavioral parity on chat lifecycle for supported providers.
2. Keep intentional Rust improvements (document, never silently revert):
   - SSRF hardening on image fetch
   - Fail-loud MissingCredentials (vs Bearer undefined)
   - Combo quarantine + disabled members + capacity pre-skip (Rust extensions — document vs optional gate)
   - Refresh dedup does NOT cache null failures (JS bug)
   - Encrypted SQLite secrets, HMAC API keys
3. Prefer wiring existing dead Rust code over rewrites.
4. Every CRITICAL/HIGH item ships with unit + e2e/regression tests and structured decision logs.

## Phase tracks (dependency order)
| Phase | Focus |
|-------|--------|
| P0-A | Translator routing, direct pairs, response intermediate hop, registration |
| P0-B | Chat pipeline order, forceStream SSE→JSON, passthrough, DeepSeek-TUI, Accept |
| P0-C | Executors: Kiro, GitHub /responses, Cursor host, Codex, orphans, Default 429/noAuth |
| P0-D | OAuth: codebuddy-cn, github/copilot, merge, shouldRefresh, kiro external_idp/vertex |
| P1-combo | RR/autoswitch order, sticky, fusion grace+stream, final status, capability detect |
| P1-caps | targetFormat/transport/upstream/strip, detectFormat, thinkingUnified, modality |
| P2 | ERROR_RULES unify, comboStrategies schema, PXPIPE, docs, hedging wire-or-doc |
| Tests | Shared parity harness with decision logging |

## Inventory of audit findings embedded (do not drop)
CRITICAL: translator direct route missing; response hop uses raw chunk; antigravity wrong fn; response pairs unregistered; normalize_claude_passthrough orphan; forceStream+SSE→JSON missing; DeepSeek-TUI always non-stream; providerThinking after translate; Kiro URL/auth/EventStream; Cursor host; GitHub /responses; grok-cli missing; mimo-free/codebuddy-cn orphans; combo autoswitch before RR; fusion grace+judge stream; OAuth codebuddy-cn/github/copilot wrong.
HIGH: no resolveTransport/model targetFormat/upstream/stripList; anthropic-compatible→openai; detectFormat order; modality caps by format; passthrough still strips; prefetch incomplete; TTS filter; PXPIPE; thinkingUnified; sticky hardcode 1; combo status.max(500); Codex force/effort/prefetch; merge expires_at; CODEX_MAX_REFRESH_AGE; needs_refresh(None); Default 429 no URL fallback; noAuth missing; dual-auth anthropic-compat; header hooks; non-SSE stream guard; gemini-cli imageGen non-stream; clear all model locks on success.

## Definition of Done (epic)
- [ ] All P0 child epics closed with their leaf Success Criteria met
- [ ] Parity harness (`…mj1.8`) runs in CI (`cargo test parity_` or equivalent) with decision logs
- [ ] Golden-path e2e (mocked upstream): Claude Code passthrough, OpenAI→Claude, Kiro EventStream→SSE, Codex stream:false→JSON, combo RR+vision primary, GitHub codex→/responses, github+codebuddy-cn refresh wire-format tests
- [ ] `docs/parity-9router.md` lists intentional divergences + dispatch matrix
- [ ] `br dep cycles` empty; no orphan executor files outside mod.rs without ADR note
- [ ] AGENTS.md beads blurb updated to point at this epic (when closing)

## Test strategy (epic-level)
- Unit: pure decision functions (format detect, stream decision, fallback rules, rotation, merge)
- Snapshot: translator request/response pairs (existing insta snapshots + new direct-route cases)
- Integration: chat.rs path with mock HTTP (wiremock/httpmock) per provider
- E2E optional live: behind `OPENPROXY_LIVE_PARITY=1`, never required for CI green
- Logging: every request logs `route=direct|pivot`, `stream=`, `forceStreamSSE2JSON=`, `executor=`, `passthrough=`, `acc=`

## Out of scope
- openproxy-bug4 (encryption key), openproxy-bug5 (/v1/models custom) — independent
- Pure dashboard UI visual parity
- Copying known 9router bugs

## Parallelization guidance
Max parallel tracks after harness exists: P0-A, P0-B (except passthrough after hooks), P0-C (except codex after forceStream, github after oauth), P0-D, P1-combo (except caps after modality), P1-caps detectFormat.

# Phase P0-A: Translator Routing & Registration

## Background
9router translator tries a direct source:target pair first, then falls back to OpenAI pivot. OpenProxy always pivots through OpenAI and ignores registered direct pairs (claude→kiro, kiro→claude). Response step-2 also feeds the original provider chunk instead of the OpenAI intermediate. Several response pairs have implementations but are not registered. openai→antigravity is registered to the wrong transform function (gemini-cli instead of antigravity).

## Why This Phase First
Almost every non-OpenAI client↔non-OpenAI provider path is broken or lossy without correct routing. Fixing executors first would still produce wrong request/response shapes.

## Scope
- Direct-route lookup for request and response
- Response double-hop intermediate chaining
- Register missing response pairs
- Fix openai→antigravity registration
- Mount prepare_claude_request / filter_to_openai_format hooks
- Unit + snapshot tests

## Files
- src/core/translator/registry.rs
- src/core/translator/request/*
- src/core/translator/response/*
- src/core/translator/snapshots/

## Success Criteria
- claude→kiro uses direct request transform (not double hop)
- kiro→claude uses direct response transform
- openai→antigravity uses openai_to_antigravity_request
- Client Claude + provider Kiro stream produces Claude-shaped SSE
- All new paths covered by unit/snapshot tests with logging of chosen route

title: Translator: direct-route request lookup (source:target first)
description:
# Implement direct-route lookup in translate_request

## Background
9router open-sse/translator/index.js (approx L77-103): if source≠target, look up requestRegistry.get(`${source}:${target}`). If found, run only that function. Otherwise pivot source→openai then openai→target.

OpenProxy src/core/translator/registry.rs translate_request always does OpenAI pivot and never looks up (source, target) even when registered (e.g. claude→kiro at registration L751+).

Without this, thinking/tool/image fidelity is lost on fragile pairs. 9router AGENTS.md explicitly warns OpenAI bridge is lossy and direct routes are preferred.

## Technical Approach
1. In TranslatorRegistry::translate_request, before pivot:
   - if source == target: normalization only (existing)
   - else if let Some(fn) = request_transforms.get(&(source, target)): run fn; then normalization; return
   - else: existing pivot
2. Log chosen path at debug: "direct source→target" vs "pivot via openai".
3. Keep apply_normalization_hooks after either path.

## Success Criteria
- Unit test: mock or real claude→kiro registration is invoked and openai→kiro is NOT when body is Claude-shaped.
- Existing OpenAI→X paths still work.
- Logging shows route selection.

## Test Plan
- Unit: registry tests for direct hit, pivot miss, same-format.
- Snapshot: claude→kiro request body fields (tool_use, thinking) preserved better than pivot (compare hashes or key fields).
- Do not regress openai→claude snapshots.

## Considerations
- Response path is separate bead.
- Do not remove pivot; many pairs only have openai bridges.
- credentials/stream args must pass through direct fn same as pivot.

title: Translator: direct-route response + intermediate hop chaining

# Implement direct-route + intermediate chaining in translate_response

## Background
JS response path (translator/index.js ~L159-195):
1. Try responseRegistry.get(`${targetFormat}:${sourceFormat}`) direct
2. Else: target→openai into results[], then for each intermediate r, openai→source

Rust translate_response (~L424-448):
1. source→OpenAI into results
2. For OpenAI→target, calls transform(chunk, state) on the ORIGINAL provider chunk, not intermediate results
3. No direct (source,target) lookup for pairs like kiro→claude

Parameter naming in chat.rs: translate_response(stream_target_format, stream_source_format, ...) matches JS provider-format-first then client-format.

## Technical Approach
1. Add direct lookup for (provider_fmt, client_fmt) when both ≠ OpenAI and pair registered.
2. Pivot: step1 provider→openai; step2 map over intermediate strings (or bytes) into client format.
3. Unit-test with a tiny synthetic transform chain.

## Success Criteria
- kiro→claude direct used when registered.
- Double-hop OpenAI intermediate is input to second transform (prove with test double that records inputs).
- Stream path in chat.rs still works with tool_name_map state.

## Test Plan
- Unit tests with fake transforms recording call order and inputs.
- Integration: mock kiro SSE bytes → Claude SSE events.
- Log path selection.

## Considerations
- State (ResponseTransformState) must remain persistent across chunks for both hops.
- Empty conversion from step1 should not invent garbage; match JS empty-array behavior.

# Phase P0-B: Chat Pipeline Order & ForceStream

## Background
9router handleChatCore has a carefully ordered pipeline. OpenProxy chat.rs reorders key steps and omits forceStream SSE→JSON, mis-handles DeepSeek-TUI streaming, injects providerThinking after translation, and never calls normalize_claude_passthrough on native Claude passthrough.

JS order (simplified):
format → bypass → transport/target → thinking → stream decision → passthrough? → modality if !passthrough → translate/normalizeClaude → tool dedupe → TTS filter → RTK → Headroom → Caveman → Ponytail → PXPIPE → execute → 401 refresh → forceStream SSE→JSON → stream/non-stream

Rust order (simplified):
auth/model → Accept mutates stream → bypass → plan → modality always → prefetch → translate → RTK → Headroom → thinking → Caveman → tool dedupe → dispatch (DeepSeek always non-stream) → 401 loop → proxy

## Scope
- Reorder thinking override before translate
- DeepSeek-TUI only force non-stream when body.stream !== true
- Wire forceStream registry + handleForcedSSEToJson path
- Wire normalize_claude_passthrough + mount claude_format module
- Skip modality strip/prefetch on passthrough
- Accept-header stream preference parity (do not override explicit stream:true)
- TTS tool filter; optional PXPIPE later (P2)

## Files
- src/server/api/chat.rs
- src/core/chat/mod.rs
- src/core/translator/request/claude_format.rs (+ mod.rs)
- src/core/media/responses/stream_to_json.rs
- provider registry / forceStream flags

## Success Criteria
- DeepSeek-TUI interactive (stream:true) receives SSE
- Claude Code passthrough runs normalize_claude_passthrough
- Codex/openai forceStream + client stream:false returns aggregated JSON
- providerThinking on/off/effort applied on source body before translate

# Fix DeepSeek-TUI stream decision to match 9router

## Background
JS chatCore.js ~L93-97:
  if (detectedTool === "deepseek-tui" && body.stream !== true) stream = false;
Comment: interactive TUI needs SSE; non-interactive (-p) cannot parse SSE.

Rust chat.rs ~L898-904:
  if client_tool == Some(DeepseekTui) { stream = false } always.

This breaks interactive DeepSeek TUI sessions that send stream:true.

## Technical Approach
Change condition to only force false when stream is not explicitly true (missing or false). Match JS strict equality on true.

Also review Accept-header mutation: Rust forces body.stream=false even when client sent stream:true if Accept prefers JSON — JS only adjusts when body.stream !== true and !providerRequiresStreaming. Align Accept logic in same bead or sibling.

## Success Criteria
- stream:true + DeepSeek-TUI UA → upstream stream true / SSE response path.
- stream absent + DeepSeek-TUI → non-stream.
- stream:false + DeepSeek-TUI → non-stream.

## Test Plan
- Unit tests on stream decision helper (extract if needed).
- E2E with mocked UA header deepseek-tui.

## Considerations
- Extract stream decision into a pure function for testability (mirrors chatCore logic block).

title: Chat: forceStream registry + SSE→JSON for non-stream clients
description:
# Implement forceStream + SSE-to-JSON aggregation path

## Background
JS: PROVIDERS[provider].forceStream === true forces stream=true upstream; if !clientRequestedStreaming && providerRequiresStreaming, handleForcedSSEToJson aggregates SSE into JSON (sseToJsonHandler.js). Providers with forceStream in 9router registry include codex, openai (some transports), commandcode, codebuddy-cn, grok-cli.

Rust: no chat-level forceStream; stream_to_json.rs exists but unused from chat.rs. Clients requesting stream:false against force-stream providers get wrong content-type/body.

clientRequestedStreaming in JS also treats antigravity/gemini/gemini-cli formats as streaming clients.

## Technical Approach
1. Add force_stream flag to provider config / registry used by chat plan.
2. Compute client_requested_streaming and provider_requires_streaming like JS.
3. When provider forces stream but client wants JSON: execute stream=true upstream, collect SSE, convert via sse_stream_to_json / convert_responses_stream_to_json, return application/json.
4. Codecs: support both chat-completions SSE and responses SSE (codex).

## Success Criteria
- Codex + stream:false returns single JSON object (not SSE).
- stream:true still streams.
- Force-stream providers listed match 9router registry intent.

## Test Plan
- Unit: sse_stream_to_json fixtures already exist — wire integration test from chat layer with mock upstream SSE.
- E2E: codex-like SSE → JSON collapse.

title: Chat: Accept-header must not override explicit stream:true

# Chat: Accept-header must not override explicit stream:true

## Background
JS chatCore.js ~L99-106: if Accept has application/json, lacks text/event-stream, body.stream !== true, and !providerRequiresStreaming → local stream=false (does not mutate body when stream explicitly true).
Rust chat.rs ~L330-341: wants_json && !wants_sse && accept != "*/*" → inserts body.stream=false even if client sent stream:true. Extra `*/*` exclusion is Rust-only.

## User impact / failure mode
AI SDK or curl clients that send both Accept: application/json and stream:true (common) incorrectly get non-streaming JSON, breaking progressive UIs.

## Technical Approach
1. Extract pure `apply_accept_stream_preference(accept, stream_field, provider_requires_streaming) -> bool`.
2. Only force false when stream is not explicitly true AND !provider_requires_streaming.
3. Prefer not mutating body; pass resolved stream flag downstream (or mutate only when field absent).
4. Integrate with forceStream bead (1.2.3): providerRequiresStreaming blocks Accept force-down.

## Success Criteria
| Accept | body.stream | forceStream | result stream |
|--------|-------------|-------------|---------------|
| application/json | true | false | true |
| application/json | absent | false | false |
| application/json | false | false | false |
| text/event-stream | absent | false | true (default) |
| application/json | false | true | true (upstream) + SSE→JSON if client non-stream |

## Test Plan
- Unit table-driven (all rows above + `*/*` + multi-value Accept).
- Integration: POST with Accept json + stream true → mock sees stream true.
- Log: `ACCEPT_STREAM prefer_json=.. resolved_stream=..`.

## Considerations
- Coordinate with DeepSeek-TUI and imageGen stream helpers — single resolve_stream_flags module preferred.
- Do not break pure JSON AI SDK clients (Accept json, no stream field).

# Model lock clear on success: selective (JS) vs clear-all (Rust)

## Background
JS clearAccountError: clears the succeeded model lock + expired locks selectively.
Rust clear_connection_error: wipes ALL modelLock_* keys on any success.
Impact: a successful request for model A re-enables model B that was 404-locked, causing flapping retries and wasted quota.

## User impact
After one success, previously 404 models are retried immediately → error storms / slower fallback.

## Technical Approach
1. Port selective clear: clear lock for the model that succeeded + purge expired keys only.
2. Keep option to clear all on explicit admin reset.
3. Align mark_connection_unavailable 404 model-specific lock (already partially present) with clear path.

## Success Criteria
- Success on model A leaves active lock on model B intact until expiry.
- Expired locks cleaned.

## Test Plan
- Unit: two model locks, success on one, assert other remains.
- Integration: 404 B, success A, next request still skips B.

# Combo: apply capability autoswitch AFTER RR rotation

## Background
JS combo.js ~L229-242: `rotatedModels = getRotatedModels(...); if (autoSwitch) reorderByCapabilities(rotatedModels, required)`.
Rust chat.rs ~L384-393 then execute rotates: **reorder first, then rotate**.

Counterexample: members [A,B,C], RR index=1, only C has vision.
- JS: rotate→[B,C,A] → autoswitch→[C,B,A]
- Rust: autoswitch→[C,A,B] → rotate→[A,B,C]

Vision requests hit non-vision primary under round-robin → 400 or useless text-only answers; different model bills than 9router.

## Technical Approach
1. Move reorder_by_capabilities to after get_rotated_models inside execute_combo_strategy* (not in chat before call).
2. Keep autoSwitch default on when caps non-empty (JS default true).
3. Port unit cases from `/tmp/9router/tests/unit/combo-autoswitch.test.js` and combo-routing.test.js.

## Success Criteria
Fixture above yields C-first under RR index=1 + vision body.

## Test Plan

- Property: for sticky=1, vision request primary has vision cap when any member has it.
- Log: `COMBO_ORDER before=.. after_rr=.. after_caps=..`.

title: Combo fusion: grace timer + judge streaming parity
description:
# Combo fusion: independent straggler grace timer + judge streaming

## Background
JS fusion: when ok panels >= minPanel, setTimeout(finish, stragglerGraceMs) independent of other panel completions; judge uses original body stream flag (preserves stream:true).
Rust fusion.rs: tightens hard_deadline but only rechecks when another future completes — no independent grace sleep; judge forces stream:false; chat returns plain JSON string body for fusion success.

Defaults (both): minPanel=2, grace=8000ms, hard=90000ms.

## User impact
- Fusion latency = slowest panel hard timeout (90s) instead of ~8s after quorum.
- Streaming clients get a single JSON blob instead of SSE → UI freezes until end.

## Technical Approach
1. tokio::select! { biased; grace_sleep => finish, panel = next => handle }
2. Preserve client stream for judge body; if stream, chat path must stream judge SSE (may need execute_single_model stream=true + proxy stream).
3. Keep panels non-stream + tools stripped + tool-history flatten.
4. Fix panel text extraction to accept array content parts (not only string content) — JS extractTextContent.
5. Config: FusionConfig from combo.extra; later nested settings (1.7.2).

## Success Criteria
- 2/3 panels done → return within grace+epsilon, not full hard timeout (unit with delayed third).
- Client stream:true → response content-type text/event-stream (or documented streaming JSON lines).
- Single panel → direct dispatch; zero ok → 503.

## Test Plan
- Unit grace timer with mock delayed futures.
- Unit text extraction array content.
- Integration fusion stream content-type.
- Port ideas from `/tmp/9router/tests/unit/combo-fusion.test.js`.
- Log: `FUSION quorum=.. grace_ms=.. judge_stream=..`.

## Considerations
- Blocks 1.7.2 schema only softly (already dep).
- Do not lose anonymized Source N judge prompt.

description:
### `P0-A1a` — Add alims-intl provider to PROVIDER_CONFIGS (default.rs)

**JS (source of truth — verbatim):**

File .tmp/9router/open-sse/providers/registry/alims-intl.js:3-31. id="alims-intl", priority=11, alias="alims-intl". transport.baseUrl="https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions", headers={}, quirks={preserveCacheControl:true}. models=[{id:"qwen3.5-plus",name:"Qwen3.5 Plus"},{id:"kimi-k2.5",name:"Kimi K2.5"},{id:"glm-5",name:"GLM 5"},{id:"MiniMax-M2.5",name:"MiniMax M2.5"},{id:"qwen3-coder-next",name:"Qwen3 Coder Next"},{id:"qwen3-coder-plus",name:"Qwen3 Coder Plus"},{id:"glm-4.7",name:"GLM 4.7"}]

**Current Rust behavior:**

N/A. src/core/executor/default.rs:24-409 PROVIDER_CONFIGS has no "alims-intl" key; DefaultExecutor::new (default.rs:585-595) returns ExecutorError::UnsupportedProvider -> chat.rs:1635-1645 returns HTTP 500. Verified no other file contains the string.

**Implementation steps:**

In src/core/executor/default.rs, inside the BTreeMap::from([...]) in PROVIDER_CONFIGS, add exactly one entry (place near the alicode-intl entry at default.rs:151-155): ("alims-intl", ProviderConfig::openai("https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions"),). Do NOT add any headers (JS headers={}). Do NOT add to any anthropic/claude-compatible list in default.rs:615-627, 700-718, 805-813, 867-915. The full endpoint URL is already present so build_url (default.rs:812) returns it unchanged. Do NOT add clinepass headers block: the default.rs:947 match on "clinepass" is the existing header hook, leave it.

**Guard test:**

In tests/executor_pool_behavior.rs add #[test] fn alims_intl_has_full_endpoint_url(): build DefaultExecutor::new("alims-intl", pool, None) (must not return Err) then assert build_url("qwen3.5-plus", false, &connection("alims-intl")) == "https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions" (the full endpoint, no /chat/completions appended).

**⚠️ Risks:**

preserveCacheControl:true is a translator/request quirk (JS translator request uses it to keep cache_control). If you add the provider only to the executor, chat works but the translator must not strip cache_control for this provider — check translator/registry request_transform routing (Format::OpenAi) does not need provider-specific handling since JS preserveCacheControl only affects alicode/cache-control injection; do not reintroduce a cache_control strip for this id. The baseUrl is the FULL endpoint (…/chat/completions already present) so is_already_endpoint (default.rs:606-612) must match on "/chat/completions" — it does. Do not append an extra /chat/completions.

**Cross-check:** ✅ **CONFIRMED** — JS claim is exactly real: .tmp/9router/open-sse/providers/registry/alims-intl.js:3-31 matches every cited value verbatim (id="alims-intl", priority=11, alias, baseUrl="https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions", headers={}, quirks={preserveCacheControl:true}, and the listed models). Rust current behavior is real: PROVIDER_CONFIGS in src/core/executor/default.rs:24-409 has no "alims-intl" key (grep confirms zero hits for alims-intl/dashscope-intl/compatible-mode in default.rs), and DefaultExecutor::new returns ExecutorError::UnsupportedProvider on lookup miss, which src/server/api/chat.rs:1635-1645 maps to HTTP 500 (status: 500 in ComboAttemptError). Impl steps would work: alicode-intl is at default.rs:151-155; ProviderConfig::openai(<full URL>) yields format="openai" with empty headers (matches JS headers={}), and since alims-intl is in no claude-beta/anthropic list (default.rs:615-627, 700-715, 805-810), build_url emits the baseUrl as-is and build_headers uses the generic Bearer branch — correct for DashScope compatible-mode. Minor inaccuracies that do not change the verdict: (1) the chat error mapping is in src/server/api/chat.rs, not "chat.rs"; DefaultExecutor::new's UnsupportedProvider return is actually at lines 581-595 not 585-595. (2) "Verified no other file contains the string" is overstated — alims-intl appears in two model-catalog data files (src/core/model/provider_catalog.json:116,4533,5874 and src/core/model/sources/9router.json:73,283), which are not executor config and don't affect behavior. (3) Flagged gap: the JS preserveCacheControl quirk is not replicable by this entry because the Rust translator hardcodes filter_to_openai_format(body, false) at registry.rs:486 for all providers, so cache_control blocks will be stripped for alims-intl (JS preserves them). This is a system-wide Rust limitation beyond a PROVIDER_CONFIGS entry and does not break the routing/transport parity P0-A1a targets; worth a follow-up task but not a blocker.

---


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement per the spec above (JS source of truth + current Rust + implementation steps)
- [ ] Guard test passes: In tests/executor_pool_behavior.rs add #[test] fn alims_intl_has_full_endpoint_url(): build DefaultExecutor::new("alims-intl", pool, None) (must not return Err) then assert build_url("qwen3.5-plus", false, &connection("alims-intl")) == "https://dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions" (the full endpoint, no /chat/completions appended).

title: codebuddy-intl OAuth device-code flow in src/oauth (executor covered by P0-A1f)
description:
### `P1-B2` — codebuddy-intl OAuth device-code flow in src/oauth (executor covered by P0-A1f)

**JS (source of truth — verbatim):**

File .tmp/9router/open-sse/providers/registry/codebuddy-intl.js:64-72. oauth={baseUrl:"https://www.codebuddy.ai",stateUrl:"https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/state",tokenUrl:"https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/token",refreshUrl:"https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/token/refresh",userAgent:"IDE/2.63.2 CodeBuddy/2.63.2",platform:"ide",pollInterval:5000}. features={usage:true,usageApikey:true}. Comment line 3: all OAuth/plugin URLs use the /v2/plugin prefix with platform=ide (CN uses platform=CLI).

**Current Rust behavior:**

src/oauth/providers.rs:307-319 has the CodeBuddy CN device-code flow (copilot.tencent.com/v2/plugin/auth/state|token|token/refresh, platform CLI). There is NO codebuddy-intl (www.codebuddy.ai) entry. oauth.rs:4217 returns unknown_provider.

**Implementation steps:**

1) In src/oauth/providers.rs add a "codebuddy-intl" OAuthProviderConfig: authorize/state url="https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/state", token_url="https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/token", refresh_url="https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/token/refresh", platform="ide", userAgent="IDE/2.63.2 CodeBuddy/2.63.2", pollInterval=5000 (device-code poll loop). 2) Model the flow on the existing codebuddy CN device-code implementation (providers.rs:307-319) but swap the base domain to www.codebuddy.ai and platform to "ide". 3) The executor side (transport headers X-Product: SaaS etc.) is P0-A1f. This is the OAuth half (parity A3).

**Guard test:**

src/oauth/tests/oauth_url_tests.rs: add codebuddy-intl asserting authorize/state URL == "https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/state" and platform == "ide".

**⚠️ Risks:**

Do NOT mix CN (copilot.tencent.com, platform CLI) with intl (www.codebuddy.ai, platform ide) — the state/token/refresh URLs differ only by host but the platform param must be 'ide'. The userAgent version string "IDE/2.63.2 CodeBuddy/2.63.2" differs from the transport User-Agent "IDE/2.108.1 CodeBuddy/2.108.1" (registry line 69 vs line 29) — keep them distinct as in JS.

**Cross-check:** ❌ **REFUTED** — JS claim REAL, Rust current behavior REAL, but the impl_steps would NOT produce parity — a required custom device-code executor is missing.

(1) JS: .tmp/9router/open-sse/providers/registry/codebuddy-intl.js:64-76 exactly matches the cited oauth config (baseUrl/stateUrl/tokenUrl/refreshUrl all www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/*, userAgent "IDE/2.63.2 CodeBuddy/2.63.2", platform "ide", pollInterval 5000) and features={usage:true,usageApikey:true}. The flow is implemented in .tmp/9router/src/lib/oauth/providers/codebuddy-intl.js.

(2) Rust: src/oauth/providers.rs:307-327 has codebuddy_cn() (copilot.tencent.com state/token/refresh, platform CLI, extra_params user_agent/platform/poll_interval). No www.codebuddy.ai anywhere in src; get_config (providers.rs:446-471) has no codebuddy-intl arm; is_device_code_provider (server/api/oauth.rs:692-706) lacks codebuddy-intl; start_oauth_flow at oauth.rs:4217 returns unknown_provider for it. Claim REAL.

(3) Parity gap — the decisive flaw: the JS CodeBuddy flow is a custom non-RFC8628 protocol. requestDeviceCode POSTs JSON "{}" to stateUrl?platform=ide with headers X-Requested-With, X-Domain, X-No-Authorization, X-No-User-Id, X-Product and parses {code,data:{state,authUrl}}; pollToken GETs tokenUrl?state=... with the same headers and maps code 11217 to authorization_pending. Rust's generic device_code::start_device_flow (src/oauth/mod.rs:109-140) only form-posts client_id+scope to authorize_url and parses RFC device_code/user_code/verification_uri fields — it sends none of the CodeBuddy headers and cannot parse the CodeBuddy JSON. poll_for_token reads only the "interval" extra_param and ignores platform/user_agent/poll_interval. There is no codebuddy-intl (or codebuddy) special-case module in src/oauth (unlike kiro.rs/qoder.rs), and token_refresh.rs would need an intl mirror of refresh_codebuddy_cn_token. Adding only an OAuthProviderConfig for codebuddy-intl would dispatch it through the generic RFC flow, which cannot complete the CodeBuddy state/poll handshake — so the described impl_steps do not achieve parity.

---


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement per the spec above (JS source of truth + current Rust + implementation steps)
- [ ] Guard test passes: src/oauth/tests/oauth_url_tests.rs: add codebuddy-intl asserting authorize/state URL == "https://www.codebuddy.ai/v2/plugin/auth/state" and platform == "ide".
- [ ] `cargo test --lib` still green (no regressions)
- [ ] Verified against `.tmp/9router` reference behavior

title: Headroom missing openai-responses + kiro format paths and size/phantom logging (G2e/F7)
description:
### `P1-B2` — Headroom missing openai-responses + kiro format paths and size/phantom logging (G2e/F7)

**JS (source of truth — verbatim):**

open-sse/rtk/headroom.js:242-332 compressWithHeadroom dispatches by format:
- format "claude" (260-273): `claudeToOpenAIRequest(model, body, false)` → if !messages[] diag "Claude request did not translate to messages[]"; callCompress → `openaiToClaudeRequest(model, {...oai, messages: data.messages}, false)`; write back `body.messages` and `body.system` if !== undefined.
- format "openai-responses" (278-297): if hasUnsafeResponsesInputForCompression(body) (any input item with a string `type` !== "message") → diag "skipped: openai-responses tool/reasoning input is not safe to compress"; else `openaiResponsesToOpenAIRequest(model, body, false)` → compress → `openaiToOpenAIResponsesRequest(model, {...oai, input: undefined, messages: data.messages}, false)`; write back `body.input`.
- format "kiro" (302-313): collectKiroHeadroomMessages projects history/currentMessage userInputMessage.systemInstruction/content/toolResults tool text + assistantResponseMessage content/tool_calls into {messages, targets}; callCompress; applyKiroHeadroomMessages verifies count + role order + non-null text then writes `target.object[target.key] = text` (diag "proxy response did not match Kiro message count" / "did not preserve Kiro message order" / "missing Kiro text content").
- OpenAI (315-327): key = "messages" or "input"; `body[key] = data.messages`.
buildCompressEndpoint (59-71): `{base}/v1/compress`. callCompress POSTs `{ messages, model }` (+`config:{compress_user_messages:true}`) with `AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs)` (default 3000), returns null + diagnostic on non-ok / missing messages[]. formatHeadroomSizeLog (343-351): `body=X→Y messages=... tools=... toolHistory=... effective=%`. isHeadroomPhantomSavings (353-359): `tokens_saved>0 && before>0 && after>0 && after >= before * (1 - 0.05)`.

**Current Rust behavior:**

src/core/rtk/headroom.rs compress_with_headroom (255-300) only dispatches "claude" (271-273) or OpenAI (276-299, key messages/input). NO openai-responses translation path, NO kiro projection path, NO diagnostics, NO buildCompressEndpoint host-masking, NO size snapshot (captureSizeSnapshot), NO formatHeadroomSizeLog, NO isHeadroomPhantomSavings. The claude path (compress_claude_body 379-442) only flattens content blocks to plain text — it does NOT call the real claudeToOpenAIRequest/openaiToClaudeRequest translators, so tool_use/tool_result/thinking blocks are dropped instead of round-tripped. Format is passed as "claude"/"openai" (chat.rs:843) — never "openai-responses"/"kiro".

**Implementation steps:**

1) In src/core/rtk/headroom.rs, add a `diagnostics: &mut HeadroomDiagnostics` (new struct with `reason: Option<String>`, `endpoint: Option<String>`, `before: Option<SizeSnapshot>`, `after: Option<SizeSnapshot>`) param to compress_with_headroom (or a parallel fn) and set diag.reason only if not already set (JS setDiagnostic).
2) Add format "openai-responses": if body.input has any item whose `type` is a non-"message" string → set reason "skipped: openai-responses tool/reasoning input is not safe to compress" and return None. Otherwise route body.input through the existing Rust responses↔openai translators (crate::core::translator::request::openai_responses::{openai_responses_to_openai_request, openai_to_openai_responses_request}) — port the JS: translate to OpenAI, call_compress, then translate back passing `input: undefined, messages: compressed` and write body["input"] = result.input.
3) Add format "kiro": project conversationState.history + currentMessage into messages (systemInstruction→role system, content→role user, toolResults[].content[].text→role tool + tool_call_id, assistantResponseMessage content→role assistant + tool_calls with `arguments: JSON.stringify(input||{})` and `id`), record targets [(object,key)], POST, verify count/role-order/text, then write text back into each target. New fn `apply_kiro_headroom_messages`.
4) Add captureSizeSnapshot: jsonBytes(body), jsonBytes(messages/input array), jsonBytes(tools), jsonBytes(toolHistory filtered by role tool/function or tool_calls.length or content block type tool_use/tool_result).
5) Add buildCompressEndpoint (strip trailing '/', append /v1/compress) + maskEndpoint (strip user:pass@, query, hash).
6) Add formatHeadroomSizeLog + isHeadroomPhantomSavings (minShrinkRatio 0.05) and call them in chat.rs after compress_with_headroom (chat.rs:853-858) for the debug log.
7) For the claude path, keep the flatten but ALSO apply the real translators if the existing Rust claude↔openai translator functions are accessible; otherwise document that the current flatten approximates it (matches JS intent that the proxy only understands OpenAI shape).

**Guard test:**

cargo test headroom_responses_shape_rejected_when_unsafe in src/core/rtk/headroom.rs: body.input containing an item with type "function_call" → compress_with_headroom(format="openai-responses") returns None and diagnostics.reason starts with "skipped:". cargo test headroom_kiro_projection_roundtrips: build a kiro body with one history tool result; assert compressed text is written back into conversationState.history[0]....toolResults[0].content[0].text. cargo test headroom_phantom_savings_detected: tokens_saved>0 with before/after sizes where after >= before*0.95 → is_phantom true.

**⚠️ Risks:**

The responses round-trip MUST pass `input: undefined` to the translator so it rebuilds input from messages instead of echoing the original — the JS comment (#1998) calls this out explicitly. Kiro apply step verifies role order and returns false (with diag) when the proxy reshuffled — never write back mismatched messages. buildCompressEndpoint keeps existing query string when URL parse fails. title: zed OAuth RSA keypair flow (oauth layer; executor base covered by P0-A1n)
description:
### `P1-B3` — zed OAuth RSA keypair flow (oauth layer; executor base covered by P0-A1n)

**JS (source of truth — verbatim):**

File .tmp/9router/open-sse/providers/registry/zed.js:54-66 (RSA flow). oauth={authorizeUrl:"https://zed.dev/native_app_signin",platform:"zed",rsaKeyExchange:true}. Comment lines 55-62: 1) App generates RSA-2048 keypair locally (PKCS#1 DER, URL-safe base64). 2) Bind random TCP port on 127.0.0.1. 3) Open https://zed.dev/native_app_signin?native_app_port={port}&native_app_public_key={pub}. 4) After login, browser redirects http://127.0.0.1:{port}/?user_id=...&access_token=... where access_token = base64(RSA-encrypted plaintext token). 5) Decrypt with private key (OAEP-SHA256, fallback PKCS1v15). No clientId/clientSecret/tokenUrl/refreshUrl — long-lived access_token, no refresh. Executor auth: "Authorization: <user_id> <access_token>" plus duplicate x-zed-cloud-token header (zed.js:32-39), baseUrl https://cloud.zed.dev/completions, forceStream, NDJSON wire protocol.

**Current Rust behavior:**

No zed OAuth in src/oauth/providers.rs; oauth.rs:4217 unknown_provider. No RSA keypair logic anywhere in src/ (the auth header shape "<user_id> <access_token>" does not exist). The executor base entry P0-A1n only makes the provider reachable with a pre-obtained token.

**Implementation steps:**

1) Add a "zed" OAuth flow in src/oauth: generate RSA-2048 keypair (use the `rsa` crate or `openssl`; PKCS#1 DER, URL-safe base64 public key). 2) Bind a random TCP port on 127.0.0.1 and open https://zed.dev/native_app_signin?native_app_port={port}&native_app_public_key={pub}. 3) On redirect http://127.0.0.1:{port}/?user_id=...&access_token=... decrypt access_token with the private key (OAEP-SHA256, fallback PKCS1v15). 4) Store user_id + plaintext token (access_token). No refresh (long-lived). 5) For the chat path, the executor must send "Authorization: <user_id> <access_token>" (two space-separated values, NOT Bearer) plus "x-zed-cloud-token": <access_token> — this requires extending DefaultExecutor with a zed-specific auth header branch (build_headers default.rs:815-982) OR a dedicated zed executor (parity A3). 6) forceStream + NDJSON/SSE translation is a follow-up (zed.js executor). Full parity is out of scope for a single pass; minimum: oauth flow + custom auth header.

**Guard test:**

oauth tests: #[test] fn zed_oauth_no_refresh_endpoint(): zed OAuthProviderConfig has no token_url/refresh_url and platform == "zed". Plus an executor test asserting the Authorization header equals "<user_id> <access_token>" format once implemented.

**⚠️ Risks:**

The auth scheme is deliberately non-standard (zed.js:33-39 comment: scheme is a marker; real value built in executor). Do NOT send "Bearer <user_id> <access_token>" — the upstream expects bare "<user_id> <access_token>". The x-zed-cloud-token header duplicates the token. RSA OAEP-SHA256 with PKCS1v15 fallback must match zed's server or decryption fails. This is the most complex of the 17; it is acceptable to land the reachability fix (P0-A1n) first and the OAuth+auth-header here.

**Cross-check:** ✅ **CONFIRMED** — JS claim is real and implemented: registry/zed.js:54-66 matches exactly (authorizeUrl https://zed.dev/native_app_signin, platform:"zed", rsaKeyExchange:true, 5-step RSA comment). The flow is fully coded, not just declared — shared/zedAuth.js createZedNativeAuthData (RSA-2048, PKCS#1 DER URL-safe base64 pub key) and decryptZedAccessToken (OAEP-SHA256 then PKCS1v15 fallback), providers/zed.js (prepareConfig/exchangeToken/postExchange), and utils/server.js (127.0.0.1 TCP listener, default port 58443, random port fallback on EADDRINUSE) — plus buildZedUserAuthHeader producing the "<user_id> <access_token>" auth header. Rust claim is real: src/oauth/providers.rs get_config dispatcher (lines 442-469) has 22 arms, none "zed" (0 matches for \bzed\b/"zed"); oauth.rs:4217 is start_oauth_flow's get_provider_config None arm returning unknown_provider. No RSA keypair generation/decryption exists in src/ — the only RSA keygen is a #[cfg(test)] helper in server/auth/oidc.rs:375 and the only OAEP usage is qoder's hardcoded-public-key SHA-1 encryption (opposite direction); "<user_id> <access_token>" has 0 hits in src/. zed is also absent from the executor registry (core/executor/provider.rs PROVIDER_REGISTRY), consistent with P0-A1n's "reachable with a pre-obtained token" framing. Impl steps are feasible and sufficient: rsa=0.9 is already a Cargo dependency, sha2 is present, and the codebase already has TcpListener-on-127.0.0.1 local-callback infra (codex fixed port, xai 56121) plus code_verifier session plumbing that can carry the encoded private key (mirroring the JS trick of flowing the private key through the codeVerifier slot). Minor nits only: the registry comment says "bind random TCP port" while the JS actually prefers fixed 58443 with random fallback, and the spec's step-4 transcription is truncated — neither affects the parity gap or the implementation path.

---


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Implement per the spec above (JS source of truth + current Rust + implementation steps)
- [ ] Guard test passes: oauth tests: #[test] fn zed_oauth_no_refresh_endpoint(): zed OAuthProviderConfig has no token_url/refresh_url and platform == "zed". Plus an executor test asserting the Authorization header equals "<user_id> <access_token>" format once implemented.
