title: 2.4 - Combo & Fusion
description:
Combo & Fusion

## Scope
Multi-model strategies: sequential fallback, round-robin rotation, parallel fusion with judge synthesis.

## Subtasks
1. Combo definition: sequential model list from user config
2. FALLBACK strategy: try models in order, retry transient (502/503/504) with cooldown delay
3. ROUND-ROBIN strategy: rotate through models with sticky limit, track rotation state
4. FUSION strategy: parallel panel executors, quorum-grace collection, judge synthesis
5. Quorum-grace: min N panel responses -> short grace window for stragglers -> proceed
6. Fusion timeout: AbortController CANCELS in-flight requests on timeout (9router: leaks HTTP requests)
7. Lone-survivor fusion: use the ONE successful panel response directly (9router: re-requests model = double cost)
8. Capability auto-switch: detect vision/pdf/search requirements, reorder models to front
9. flattenToolHistory: convert tool turns to prose but assign role:user (9router: role:assistant creates consecutive assistants)

## CRITICAL 9router Fixes
- Fusion timeout LEAKS in-flight HTTP requests: no AbortController passed. Fix: pass cancel signal.
- Lone-survivor discards panel response, re-requests model. Fix: return existing response directly.
- flattenToolHistory creates consecutive assistant roles (tool->assistant). Fix: assign role:user or merge.
- Rotation state migration path incomplete: old {index} format causes NaN. Fix: check both formats.
- checkFallbackError in combo called WITHOUT backoffLevel. Fix: propagate backoff level.
- 429 cascade no delay. Fix: apply cooldownMs before next model.

## Files
- src/combo/strategy.rs — ComboStrategy enum + dispatch
- src/combo/fallback.rs — Sequential fallback
- src/combo/round_robin.rs — Round-robin with rotation state
- src/combo/fusion.rs — Parallel panel + judge synthesis
- src/combo/capability.rs — Required capabilities detection

## Tests
- Fallback tries models in order, stops on success
- Round-robin distributes evenly with sticky limit
- Fusion panel timeout cancels in-flight requests
- Lone-survivor returns existing result (no re-request)
- Capability auto-switch reorders vision models for image requests
- Rate limit delay prevents cascade

title: 2.1 - Provider Credential Management
description:
Provider Credential Management

## Scope
Manage per-provider credentials with encrypted storage. Multi-account strategies and thread-safe selection.

## Subtasks
1. Credential storage: provider_id, auth_type (api_key, oauth, device_code), encrypted tokens, metadata
2. Fill-first strategy: sort by priority, pick first available
3. Round-robin with sticky limit: N consecutive requests to same account before rotating
4. Thread-safe account selection with tokio::sync::Mutex (not Promise-based: 9router mutex stuck bug)
5. Mutex MUST resolve in all paths: success, error, panic (9router: finally block missing)
6. Per-provider strategy overrides (fill-first per provider, round-robin per another)

## 9router CRITICAL Fixes
- Mutex stuck on exception: resolveMutex never called. Fix: use tokio::sync::Mutex RAII guard.
- Race between account selection and lock write: selected, then locked outside mutex. Fix: lock inside transaction.
- _connection live reference: concurrent updateProviderConnection causes stale reads. Fix: deep clone or read-latest.
- appending consecutiveUseCount outside mutex: clearAccountError/markAccountUnavailable bypass mutex. Fix: all writes through guarded methods.

## Files
- src/credentials/mod.rs — CredentialManager struct + strategies
- src/credentials/storage.rs — Encrypted storage (delegates to DB layer)
- src/credentials/selection.rs — Account selection algorithms

## Tests
- Fill-first picks highest priority available account
- Round-robin distributes evenly with sticky limit
- Mutex resolves in error path (inject panic in selection)
- Concurrent selection returns different accounts

title: [BUG] OPENPROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY mismatch causes encrypted keys to be sent to upstream
description:
## Bug
In `src/db/mod.rs`:
- **Write** (`update`, line 141): `encryption_key().unwrap_or_default()` → uses empty string `""` when env var unset
- **Read** (`read_app_db`, line 498): `if let Some(ref key) = encryption_key()` → SKIPS decryption when env var unset

Net effect: encrypted-with-empty-key blob is stored, then read back AS-IS (no decryption), and the encrypted blob is then sent as the upstream API key. Upstream returns "Invalid API key" / "Invalid token".

## Additional symptom
Each subsequent save RE-ENCRYPTS the already-encrypted blob, causing `apiKey` field to grow monotonically (472 → 920 → ...) on every restart.

## Fix
Set `OPENPROXY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` consistently when starting both the CLI (for setup) and the server (for runtime). Use the SAME value or encryption will be inconsistent.

## Files
- src/db/mod.rs (write uses `unwrap_or_default`)
- src/db/crypto.rs (read skips decryption if key is None)
- Suggested improvement: make write also use the key if env var is set (or fail loudly if both write and read should agree)

title: P0 authz: split requireApiKey out of require_login on the /v1 gate
description:
17 of the 58 confirmed P0 findings are authorization. The root cause is one conflation:

OpenProxy keys the /v1/* API-key gate on settings.requireLogin — a DASHBOARD-AUTH flag — so a user who wants the dashboard locked also locks every API client, and a user who leaves the dashboard open leaves /v1 open. 9router has these as two independent settings. Concretely:
  - no requireApiKey setting exists, so the dashboard's "Require API key" toggle
    (OpenProxy src/types/mod.rs Settings / UpdateSettings) is a no-op
  - POST /v1/videos/edits and /v1/videos/extensions skip the API-key check
    entirely on the multipart / non-JSON path
  - /v1beta/models is unauthenticated while /v1/models is not (the audit verdict:
    9router also leaves it open, so this one is NOT in scope — do not add auth
    there, it would break Gemini CLI)
  - GET /v1/models, /v1/models/info and the disabled-model filter interact with
    the same gate

Every finding cites both sides; the full evidence text with file:line on each side
is in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search by 'requireLogin' or 'requireApiKey').

FIX: add requireApiKey to Settings, default it to match 9router, wire it to the
dashboard toggle, and gate /v1/* on it instead of requireLogin. Keep the
dashboard's own gate on requireLogin. Fix the videos multipart path in the same
bead or a sibling.

VERIFY: with requireLogin=true and requireApiKey=false, a dashboard-unlocked
setup must still serve /v1 with a valid client key and reject without one; with
requireApiKey=true and requireLogin=false, the reverse. Cover the videos
multipart path explicitly.
close_reason: Fixed in 100ebf6b, and the bead's premise needed correcting. requireApiKey ALREADY existed as Settings::require_api_key (Option<bool>, falling back to require_login only for a pre-field settings blob) and the dashboard toggle was ALREADY wired at EndpointPageClient.tsx:413. So the settings-add and toggle parts of the FIX were done. What remained: the media surface still read require_login - the exact conflation - in generic_media_handler and video_create_handler, and video_edits_extensions_proxy had NO auth check at all because it takes the raw request rather than Json<Value> and so never reached the shared gate; both its JSON and multipart arms were reachable with no key. All three now gate on require_api_key(), the video proxy before it branches on content type. /v1beta/models is deliberately untouched per the bead's own warning that adding auth there would break Gemini CLI. Tests set the two knobs to opposite values so a handler reading the wrong one cannot pass by accident; both are proven to fail when reverted. 2292 lib tests pass; the 3 pre-existing run_command_with_timeout failures remain.

title: SSE stream lifecycle (chat.rs + stream handling)
description:
PART OF A SPLIT, re-filed by polish round 3 — the original area clustering mis-binned findings by subsystem. CHECK THE WORKING TREE FIRST: several predate fixes that have since landed, and some were duplicates of a sibling bead's item, now removed.

COMPLETION RULE: this is a WORK LIST. Every finding is confirmed and in scope. If you believe one is unreachable, PROVE it by naming the guard and delete the finding. 'Low value' is not a reason.

9router is canonical, including its quirks, unless the finding says the quirk is the defect. Evidence for every finding is in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md — search by the location below.

--- FINDINGS ---
1. [P1] 9router: open-sse/config/runtimeConfig.js:53 + open-sse/providers/registry/qoder.js:23 + open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingHandler.js:87; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:110
   GAP: OpenProxy hard-codes a 180 s stall timeout for every provider; 9Router uses 360 s by default and 120 s for Qoder.
2. [P1] 9router: open-sse/handlers/chatCore/sseToJsonHandler.js:228-230, 261-269, 275-283; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:3442-3507 (esp. 3503) and src/core/media/responses/stream_to_json.rs:445-530
   GAP: OpenProxy's forced-SSE->JSON collapse always emits a `chat.completion`, with no Responses-object branch and no Gemini `candidates` envelope branch.
3. [P1] 9router: open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingHandler.js:62-80; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:3756-3794 (esp. 3760-3762, 3767-3769, 3792)
   GAP: Three divergences: OpenProxy rejects `application/json` (9Router allows it), always returns HTTP 502 (9Router echoes the upstream status, so a 200 HTML intercept stays 200), and slices a `String` at byte offset 500 which panics on a non-cha
4. [P1] 9router: open-sse/utils/responsesStreamHelpers.js:29-31 + 34-49, open-sse/utils/stream.js:256-280 + 465-480, open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingHandler.js:85-86, open-sse/utils/streamHandler.js:104-112 + 155-163; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:3924-3926 + 3959-3971
   GAP: OpenProxy never synthesizes the `response.failed` + `data: [DONE]` terminal for a Responses-API stream that ends, stalls, or is aborted before a terminal event.
5. [P1] 9router: open-sse/utils/stream.js:60 + 110-112; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:4169-4170, openai_to_claude.rs:120, openai_responses.rs:1323 + 1371, claude_to_openai.rs:397
   GAP: OpenProxy decodes each HTTP chunk in isolation instead of with a streaming decoder, so a multi-byte UTF-8 character split across a chunk boundary is corrupted into U+FFFD replacement characters.
6. [P1] 9router: open-sse/utils/streamHandler.js:155-163 + 202-210, open-sse/handlers/chatCore/streamingHandler.js:72; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:3869-3872, 3936-3939, 4027-4030, 4075-4078
   GAP: On a stall or mid-stream transport error OpenProxy injects a `data: {"error":...}` SSE frame into the live stream; 9Router just closes the stream.
7. [P1] open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:291-300 + open-sse/rtk/pxpipe.js:32 vs src/server/api/chat.rs:1322-1423 (+ src/types/mod.rs:616, src/server/api/pxpipe.rs:52)
   GAP: OpenProxy's PXPIPE toggle is a no-op for request bodies — the service can be installed and started, but no request is ever transformed by it.
8. [P1] src/server/api/chat.rs:3756-3795
   GAP: The non-SSE stream guard triggers on a different content-type set, hard-codes 502 instead of the upstream status, and stops sanitising the message text.
9. [P1] src/server/api/chat.rs:3766-3771
   GAP: The non-SSE guard truncates a Rust `String` by byte index and panics on a non-UTF-8 boundary.
10. [P1] src/server/api/chat.rs:3851-3943 (no terminal synthesis)
   GAP: When a Responses passthrough stream ends without a terminal event, OpenProxy never emits `response.failed` + `[DONE]`.
11. [P1] src/server/api/chat.rs:4839-4848, 4884-4897
   GAP: Error responses produced through the raw-body passthrough carry no `Content-Type` header at all.
12. [P2] 9router open-sse/services/combo.js:371-375 + open-sse/utils/error.js:116-128; OpenProxy src/server/api/chat.rs:4827-4869
   GAP: OpenProxy's final combo-failure message never carries the human-readable `(reset after ...)` suffix that 9router appends.
13. [P2] 9router: open-sse/utils/stream.js:88-93, 197-200, 320-321; openproxy: src/server/api/chat.rs:3850, 3876, 4148-4150
   GAP: OpenProxy records streaming usage from the single last raw chunk only; 9Router merges usage across every chunk and falls back to an estimate.
14. [P2] SSE stall watchdog timeout
   GAP: OpenProxy's SSE stall timeout is a hardcoded 180 s applied to all providers, versus 9router's 360 s default with a 120 s per-provider Qoder override — and OpenProxy's own correct 360 s constant is dead code.
15. [P3] SSE response headers on the streamed path
   GAP: OpenProxy adds `X-Accel-Buffering: no` to client-facing SSE (9Router reserves that for the internal no-buffer variant) and assembles the header set inline rather than from 9Router's single table.
16. [P3] open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:238-242 vs src/server/api/chat.rs:1323 vs :1415-1423
   GAP: For TTS models OpenProxy compresses (and bills) tool content that it deletes two steps later, so the recorded compression stats for TTS requests are non-zero where 9Router records none.

COUNT: 16 ({'P1': 11, 'P2': 3, 'P3': 2}).

title: test: the dispatch-loop bound tests do not actually prove the fix
description:
openproxy-i8fi shipped an attempt budget and a refreshed_this_request set, both correct. Its three tests in tests/dispatch_loop_bound.rs pin the CONTRACT, not the failure: an integration review disabled BOTH guards (budget raised to +1,000,000; refreshed set emptied) and all three still passed.

The tests exercise the guard's observable contract rather than a request that would otherwise hang forever.

FIX: add a dispatcher harness that, with the guards removed, would loop indefinitely, and assert it terminates within a timeout. A test with a wall-clock timeout is the only shape that actually distinguishes the fix from its absence. Keep the existing contract tests — they are worth having — but stop treating them as the regression guard.

title: P1: dashboard reports success for failed ops (optimistic toggles, missing error states, 200+success:false endpoints)
description:
P1 (elevated by blast radius: this is the "the dashboard lies to you" batch). Core surfaces #1 and #2.

THE PATTERN: the dashboard reports success for operations that failed. Across the providers UI there is a consistent failure mode — optimistic state flip, fetch, no res.ok check, no rollback, no error surfaced to the user, and the component's store is never refreshed.

CONFIRMED INSTANCES:
 1. web/src/components/providers/ProvidersPageClient.tsx:312-314 flips the provider-card on/off optimistically, :315-323 fires N PUTs inside Promise.allSettled and DISCARDS the result. No res.ok, no rollback, no notify.error. The card shows the wrong state until a manual reload. (Mirror the correct pattern at ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:921-933.)
 2. ProvidersPageClient.tsx:142-175 the mount fetch has NO error state. Both a thrown error and a non-ok response leave connections = [] (:104, :155), so all ~150 cards render the literal "No connections" (:56, :1074). hasAnyResult (:562) is computed from the static catalog, which suppresses the empty state entirely. Session expiry (401 from require_dashboard_session, src/server/auth/mod.rs:236-240) is the routine trigger, and the dashboard HTML is not auth-gated. The user is shown a confident empty list rather than "please sign in again".
 3. ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:288-292 — same shape on the detail page: a failed fetch becomes "No connections yet" plus a working Add-Connection CTA, or "Provider not found" for a compatible node (:1316-1325).
 4. Ten detail-page mutation handlers swallow every failure into console.log: ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:313, 356, 382, 670, 690, 724, 802, 818, 1025, plus four in ModelsCard.tsx:162-198. Several have no !res.ok branch at all. `notify` is already imported (:101) and used correctly at :681-684 and :795 two lines away — this is oversight, not design.
 5. AddCustomModelModal ALWAYS closes: ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:1890-1893 awaits a callee that never throws (:704-722, where the !res.ok branch does not rethrow and the catch is console.log-only), so the typed id is destroyed on failure and on network failure there is no toast at all. ModelsCard.tsx:301-304 is worse — no !res.ok branch anywhere. Make the callee return a boolean; close only on success.
 6. ProviderDetailPageClient.tsx:976 bulk delete filters by the unfiltered idsToDelete while the toast at :978-986 reports the real failure count, and there is no fetchConnections() re-sync (contrast ProxyPoolsPageClient.tsx:252-257). Reachable on 401, where every row simply vanishes.
 7. handleSwapPriority (:840-851) has no res.ok check, but the real defect is server-side: GET /api/providers without a query hits the un-paginated branch (src/server/api/mod.rs:970-976) which returns raw slice order, and AppDb::normalize() never re-sorts. Priority order only reappears after a restart (export.rs:47 re-ORDER BY priority). Fix the ordering, and add the missing res.ok check.
 8. The dev "mock all" toggle has no failure path (ProvidersPageClient.tsx:571-583) and the banner (:587-603) is driven by local forceAll rather than re-reading /api/mock/status — after a SUCCESSFUL toggle the badges stay stale until reload. SimulationModeToggle.tsx:70-73 does this correctly; copy it.

SERVER-SIDE CONTRACT TOO (these are why the client cannot detect the failure):
 9. Disable/Enable endpoints return HTTP 200 with {"success":false} on DB failure: src/server/api/models_disabled.rs:160-163 and :213-216. The client (availableModels.ts:482-497, :499-514, :520-530) checks neither res.ok nor success, and its `catch { // ignore }` can never fire on a 200 — so confirmDisableAll always reaches notify.success and its catch is DEAD CODE. Return 500 on failure; make the client check res.ok AND success. The same 200+success:false pattern exists at models_alias.rs:324, models_custom.rs:169 and :193, provider_filters.rs:109 and :187 — fix all of them.
 10. Deleting a compatible provider node orphans its connection and custom models: src/server/api/provider_nodes.rs:238 retains only db.provider_nodes. The connection stays in /api/providers and in filter_available_accounts (src/core/account_fallback/mod.rs:654) with no UI left to find or remove it. Add the two retain calls and say so in the confirmation copy.

VERIFICATION: for each surface, force the failure (expire the session for the 401 cases, point at a returning 500 for the rest) and assert the user sees a real error and the UI does not claim a state the backend rejected. The "Disable All" case is the highest-value one because it is the exact path a user relies on to stop a model from being billed.

REMEMBER: cd web && pnpm build.

title: Executor: implement grok-cli (cli-chat-proxy Grok Build)
description:
# Executor: implement grok-cli (Grok Build / cli-chat-proxy)

## Background
9router has a specialized executor `open-sse/executors/grok-cli.js` + registry `providers/registry/grok-cli.js` for **Grok CLI / Grok Build** on `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/responses`.

This is **not** the same product as:
- `xai` → `api.x.ai` (API key / Grok Build OAuth PKCE, already partially ported as `xai.rs`)
- `grok-web` → grok.com web SSO cookie (`grok_web.rs`)

Deep scan after closing the 9router-parity epic found `grok-cli` completely missing from OpenProxy:
- No `src/core/executor/grok_cli.rs`
- Not in `executor/mod.rs`
- Not in `chat.rs` dispatch
- Aliases `gcli`, `grok-build`, `gb` unhandled

## JS surface (must match)
- **URL**: `https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/responses` (Responses API)
- **forceStream**: true (registry) → chat forceStream + SSE→JSON path already exists
- **Auth**: OAuth device-code; Bearer access token; headers:
  - `User-Agent: grok-pager/0.2.93 grok-shell/0.2.93 (linux; x86_64)`
  - `x-xai-token-auth: xai-grok-cli`
  - `x-grok-client-identifier: grok-pager`
  - `x-grok-client-version: 0.2.93`
  - `x-authenticateresponse: authenticate-response`
  - plus turn/session headers (`x-grok-turn-idx`, session/machine ids) from executor
- **OAuth**: client_id `b1a00492-073a-47ea-816f-4c329264a828`, device/token URLs on `auth.x.ai`, scope includes `grok-cli:access`
- **Body**: Responses allowlist; strip server item refs when `store=false`; normalize tools (flatten function + keep hosted web_search/x_search); effort suffix `-high|-medium|-low` → reasoning effort; upstream model id via catalog
- **Refresh**: via `refreshProviderCredentials("grok-cli", …)` / same token URL as xai with grok-cli scope

## Technical Approach
1. Port provider registry entry (models, forceStream, oauth metadata, aliases).
2. New `GrokCliExecutor` (specialized, not Default): build URL, headers, transform request (Responses shape, effort strip, tool normalize, strip stored refs).
3. Wire into `executor/mod.rs` + `chat.rs` dispatch for `grok-cli` / `gcli` / `grok-build` / `gb`.
4. OAuth login + `dispatch_oauth_refresh` arm for `grok-cli` (may share xai token endpoint with correct client_id/scope).
5. Ensure forceStream list includes `grok-cli`.
6. Unit tests: URL, headers (no secrets logged), effort strip, tool flatten, turn-idx monotonicity.

## Success Criteria
- `provider=grok-cli` (and aliases) hits specialized executor, not Default/xai/grok-web.
- Upstream URL is cli-chat-proxy `/v1/responses`.
- stream:false client still works via existing SSE→JSON path.
- OAuth refresh updates access token for grok-cli connections.
- Models `grok-4.5(-high|-medium|-low)` resolve effort + upstream id correctly.

## Test Plan
- Unit: header builder, effort resolution, tool normalize, strip server ids.
- Mock HTTP: assert path `/v1/responses` and required headers.
- Integration: forceStream SSE→JSON for stream:false.
- Log: `EXECUTOR provider=grok-cli mode=responses force_stream=true`.

## Considerations
- Do not conflate with `xai` or `grok-web` — separate product surfaces.
- Reuse Codex/Responses helpers where shapes overlap; keep Grok-specific headers and turn store.
- Reference: `/tmp/9router/open-sse/executors/grok-cli.js`, `providers/registry/grok-cli.js`.

title: Executor: complete xiaomi-tokenplan dual-transport (Claude path)
description:
# Executor: complete xiaomi-tokenplan dual-transport (Claude path)

## Background
Partial port already exists in OpenProxy DefaultExecutor:
- Region sgp/cn/ams base URL resolution
- Always `{base}/chat/completions` + Bearer

9router `XiaomiTokenplanExecutor` also switches on `credentials.runtimeTransport.format === "claude"`:
- Claude → `{base without /v1}/anthropic/v1/messages` + `x-api-key` + Claude headers
- OpenAI → `{base}/chat/completions` + Bearer

Also: `resolve_transport` static table does **not** include `xiaomi-tokenplan` (or `xiaomi-mimo`), so Claude clients never get native transport and always pivot/translate.

Distinct from `mimo-free` (free JWT bootstrap).

## Technical Approach
1. Add `xiaomi-tokenplan` (+ alias `xmtp` if used) to `provider_transports` / resolve_transport with openai + claude endpoints per region (region from PSD; default sgp).
2. In DefaultExecutor `build_url` for xiaomi-tokenplan: if runtime_transport format is Claude (or path indicates anthropic), use `/anthropic/v1/messages` and strip trailing `/v1`.
3. Auth: Claude transport → `x-api-key` (raw key); OpenAI → Bearer.
4. Wire alias `xmtp` in chat/default if missing.
5. Unit: region × format URL matrix; header scheme matrix.

## Success Criteria
- sgp+claude → `https://token-plan-sgp.xiaomimimo.com/anthropic/v1/messages`
- cn+openai → `https://token-plan-cn.xiaomimimo.com/v1/chat/completions`
- Claude client to xiaomi-tokenplan uses native Claude format (passthrough or targetFormat claude) without OpenAI pivot when transport matches.

## Test Plan
Unit build_url + resolve_transport; log `XIAOMI_TOKENPLAN region= format= url=`.

## Considerations
API keys are cluster-specific; wrong region fails auth. Keep known-host allowlist.

The Rust port has NO video generation module anywhere in src/ - only image gen and TTS exist under src/server/api/media.rs. This is a full feature port, the single largest missing feature in this audit range.

Steps:
1. Read the full JS implementation (git show 3288bbc4, browse resulting files in .tmp/9router): request/response shape, async job submit -> poll -> result model, the two backends (OpenRouter passthrough vs Vertex AI Veo native API).
2. Include job-id/model-id path-injection validation from the start (da6aa901 exists because job/model ids could escape the URL path - reject traversal payloads like ../, %2e%2e, embedded / before building upstream URLs).
3. Implement Rust equivalent: new executor module, request/response types, route/handler alongside image/TTS in src/server/api/media.rs (or sibling).
4. Add video-capable models to provider_catalog.json / 9router.json with correct capability flags.

Acceptance: job-id/model-id sanitization unit tests; request/response translation unit tests for both backends; integration test of full submit -> poll -> result flow against mocked upstream.

Note: may need new async job-polling infra in the Rust executor framework - flag scope for discussion before implementing.

title: media/video/embeddings streaming
description:
Re-filed by polish round 4. CHECK THE WORKING TREE FIRST: several findings predate fixes that have
since landed, and duplicates of a sibling bead's item were removed at this pass.

COMPLETION RULE: this is a WORK LIST. Every finding is confirmed and in scope. If you believe one is
unreachable, PROVE it by naming the guard and delete the finding. 'Low value' is not a reason.

9router is canonical, including its quirks, unless the finding says the quirk is the defect. Evidence
for every finding is in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md — search by the location below.

--- FINDINGS ---
1. [P1] Embeddings upstream-error HTTP status
   GAP: OpenProxy re-derives the HTTP status from the upstream error text instead of passing the upstream status through.
2. [P1] Provider node validation — custom embedding
   GAP: Custom-embedding nodes are validated with GET /embeddings instead of POST, and the embedding dimension count is never returned.
3. [P2] 9router: src/app/api/v1/models/info/route.js:18-40 · openproxy: src/server/api/v1_models.rs:16-33, :679-702
   GAP: `/v1/models/info` never returns the embedding dimension count (nor `owned_by`, nor the per-kind `endpoint`), so a client cannot size its vector index from the router's own metadata.
4. [P2] Embeddings upstream request timeout
   GAP: OpenProxy allows a hung embeddings upstream to occupy the request for 180 s where 9router aborts at 60 s.
5. [P2] Embeddings upstream-error message content
   GAP: OpenProxy returns the whole raw upstream error body instead of the extracted `error.message`, and uses an `HTTP n:` prefix instead of 9router's `[n]:` form.
6. [P3] Embeddings `dimensions` field coercion
   GAP: OpenProxy silently drops a `dimensions` value that 9router coerces and forwards.
7. [P1] 9router: open-sse/handlers/embeddingsCore.js:106-114 (single retry, only on new credentials) vs OpenProxy: src/core/media/embeddings/handler.rs:78-140 (unconditional re-fire of the original request)
   GAP: OpenProxy re-fires the upstream request unconditionally after a 401/403, including when no refresh was possible, so every auth failure costs a duplicate identical request that 9router never makes.
8. [P2] 9router: open-sse/handlers/embeddingsCore.js:85-117 · openproxy: src/core/media/embeddings/handler.rs:78-140
   GAP: When a 401/403 arrives and there is no refresh token, OpenProxy re-POSTs the identical request to the upstream, doubling the number of upstream calls that 9router makes.
9. [P2] 9router: src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:73-76 (+ open-sse/handlers/embeddingsCore.js:25-27, pinned by tests/unit/embeddingsCore.test.js:415-425) · openproxy: src/core/media/embeddings/handler.rs:38-45 + src/server/api/media.rs:470-482
   GAP: An empty-string `input` is rejected locally with 400 by 9router but forwarded to the provider by OpenProxy (and `null`/`0` yield a different 400 message).
10. [P1] 9router open-sse/handlers/videoCore.js:181-184  ⟷  openproxy src/server/api/media.rs:903-917
   GAP: When the upstream video provider returns a non-2xx, OpenProxy relays the provider's own error body and headers verbatim instead of wrapping it in the `{error:{message,type,code}}` envelope with a `[provider] ` prefix and 2000-char cap that
11. [P1] 9router open-sse/handlers/videoCore.js:182-183 vs OpenProxy src/server/api/media.rs:897-918
   GAP: OpenProxy does not truncate upstream video error bodies to 2000 characters and does not prefix them with the provider name.
12. [P1] 9router open-sse/handlers/videoCore.js:9, :47-53, :99 vs OpenProxy src/server/api/media.rs:1183-1191, :1506-1510, :1377-1391
   GAP: Video upstream requests have no 120-second deadline and no 408 timeout response; they inherit an unspecified client-pool timeout and report every transport failure as 502.
13. [P1] 9router src/sse/handlers/videoGeneration.js:135,149,171,177 + src/sse/services/auth.js:110-134  ⟷  openproxy src/server/api/media.rs:726-742, 1302
   GAP: The video create path keeps no account-cooldown, model-lock or rate-limit state — it neither records failures nor skips accounts that are already known to be down, and it never returns a 429 with Retry-After.
14. [P1] 9router src/sse/handlers/videoGeneration.js:44-53 vs OpenProxy src/server/api/media.rs:1183-1187, :1506-1510
   GAP: OpenProxy gates the video endpoints on require_login instead of 9router's requireApiKey, so the two independent 9router settings are collapsed into one and the video-specific flag does not exist.
15. [P1] 9router src/sse/handlers/videoGeneration.js:97-104  ⟷  openproxy src/server/api/media.rs:1477, 1628
   GAP: The response header that pins a video job to the account that created it is named `x-openproxy-connection-id` in OpenProxy versus `x-9router-connection-id` in 9router, so a 9router-shaped client reads undefined and cannot pin the poll.
16. [P1] 9router: src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:17-24, :137-150 · openproxy: src/server/api/media.rs:533-544 (early return) vs :610-673 (usage tracking)
   GAP: Exact embedding token usage is never recorded for any provider that has an embedding adapter, so embeddings are absent from OpenProxy's usage history, cost accounting and quota views.
17. [P1] 9router: src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:56 (settings.requireApiKey gate) vs OpenProxy: src/server/api/media.rs:464 (settings.require_login gate)
   GAP: OpenProxy guards /v1/embeddings with the dashboard-login setting and has no requireApiKey setting at all, so the API-key toggle in the dashboard is a silent no-op and the two auth concerns 9router keeps separate are collapsed into one.
18. [P1] 9router: src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:73-76 (body.input check) vs OpenProxy: src/server/api/media.rs:470-482 (no input check before routing) + src/core/media/embeddings/handler.rs:38-45 (falsy-check divergence)
   GAP: OpenProxy defers the required-field check until after model resolution and adapter selection, does not apply 9router's falsy semantics, and performs no input validation at all on the non-adapter path.
19. [P1] POST /v1/videos/edits and /v1/videos/extensions — non-JSON (raw passthrough) path
   GAP: OpenProxy's raw multipart edits/extensions path has no `x-connection-id` pin, no account rotation on 401/403/429, and no 401/403 token-refresh retry, all of which 9Router applies uniformly to the same requests.
20. [P2] 9router open-sse/handlers/videoCore.js:40, :188-208 vs OpenProxy src/server/api/media.rs:1700-1732, :1025-1052
   GAP: OpenProxy omits the Accept: application/json request header on xAI/OpenRouter video calls and echoes the full upstream response header set instead of only Content-Type.
21. [P2] 9router open-sse/handlers/videoProviders/vertex.js:75-84, 148  ⟷  openproxy src/server/api/media.rs:1860, 2083-2097
   GAP: The Vertex request translation and its pre-flight validation test for key presence where 9router tests for a non-null, non-empty value, so explicit nulls and empty strings are forwarded into the Vertex `parameters` object and can defeat the
22. [P2] 9router src/sse/handlers/videoGeneration.js:177-186, :234-236 vs OpenProxy src/server/api/media.rs:1459-1479, :1624-1630
   GAP: OpenProxy's video path does not record failures or cooldowns in the shared account-fallback state, so a rate-limited video account is not excluded from later selection.
23. [P3] 9router open-sse/handlers/videoCore.js:39-45 + videoProviders/openrouter.js:11-17  ⟷  openproxy src/server/api/media.rs:1700-1731, 843-856
   GAP: The xAI and OpenRouter video requests omit the `Accept: application/json` header that 9router always sends, and the OpenRouter poll sends a Content-Type header on a bodyless GET that 9router omits.
24. [P2] Idempotency-Key on the 401 -> refresh -> retry create
   GAP: OpenProxy drops the `Idempotency-Key` on the post-refresh retry create; 9Router re-sends it on every attempt.
25. [P2] 9router: open-sse/handlers/embeddingsCore.js:32-38 (+ embeddingProviders/index.js:25-31) · openproxy: src/core/media/embeddings/mod.rs:46-68, src/server/api/media.rs:533-544, :546, :790-800, :830-841
   GAP: For a provider with no embedding adapter 9router refuses locally with a clear 400, while OpenProxy issues a live POST to a nonsense URL built by appending `/embeddings` to the provider's chat-completions endpoint.
26. [P2] 9router: open-sse/handlers/embeddingsCore.js:33-38 + src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:78-82 (explicit 400s) vs OpenProxy: src/core/media/embeddings/mod.rs:30 / 66 + src/server/api/media.rs:1092-1101 (silent fall-through to the generic proxy)
   GAP: OpenProxy has no unsupported-provider rejection for embeddings — an unrecognised provider silently falls through to a generic proxy that POSTs the request (and the API key) to a guessed api.<provider>.com URL instead of returning the named

title: P0 embeddings: rotate across credentials on auth/quota failure
description:
OpenProxy's /v1/embeddings makes exactly ONE upstream attempt on one arbitrarily-chosen priority-ordered connection and returns its error. 9router rotates through credentials on failure (.tmp/9router/src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:97-164), so a single quota-limited or revoked account fails the whole request even when a second account would serve it.

Split out of the old bead because the rotation fix changes DISPATCH behaviour on a shared handler, which reaches more than embeddings; the metering half is a separate 60-line block and should not block on it.

EVIDENCE: docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'embeddings'). The rotation site is src/server/api/media.rs:518 and :713-721 — note it is a SHARED handler, so state plainly in the bead whether the change is scoped to the embeddings route only or applies to every route that uses it, and why.

FIX: rotate to the next eligible connection on auth/quota failure, matching 9router's loop, and return the last error only when every connection fails.

VERIFY: wiremock first credential 401, second 200 -> 200 served by the second; all credentials 401 -> the 401 is returned, not a generic error.
close_reason: Fixed in 32a70f11. The media handler made one attempt against one priority-ordered connection and returned its error; select_media_connections already returned the full ordered list and was simply asked for its head element. The handler now walks the list and rotates on 401/403/429, returning the last error only when every credential has been tried. The attempt body moved unchanged into execute_media_provider_on_connection; because axum's Response exposes its status, the loop decides without threading a status out of the dozens of return paths inside. Rotation is scoped to auth/quota on purpose - a 400 or 5xx is the request's own problem and retrying it per account would multiply latency for an identical answer. SCOPE, as the bead asked: the change lives in execute_media_provider, which is the shared handler for every media route (embeddings, images, speech, search), not embeddings alone - 9router rotates the same way on videoGeneration, and all of these share the same one-connection limitation. tests/media_credential_rotation.rs covers both arms the bead specified (first 401 then 200 -> 200; all 401 -> the real 401 survives). The rotation arm is proven to fail without the fix. 2292 lib tests pass; the 3 pre-existing run_command_with_timeout failures remain.

title: P0: bound the provider dispatch loop (no break, no attempt budget on 401/403 refresh)
description:
P0 BLOCKER. Confirmed by the reviewer by measuring the loop structure of forward_with_provider_fallback (src/server/api/chat.rs:1311-2700): loop=1, break=0, continue=6, return=9. There is NO `break` and no attempt counter in the dispatch loop. The only exits are `return`.

THE DEFECT: on a 401/403 the code attempts an OAuth refresh. If the refresh SUCCEEDS it updates the connection in the DB and then `continue`s (chat.rs:~2530) WITHOUT inserting that connection into the `excluded` set and without incrementing any budget. At the top of the loop `select_connection` is free to pick the same connection again.

If the upstream keeps returning 401 while the refresh endpoint keeps succeeding — a revoked-but-refreshable account, a provider that 401s on scope, a token the provider accepts then rejects — the loop never terminates. The client request hangs forever holding a worker and a connection slot. This is a denial-of-service against the router itself, not a slow path.

THE FIX (pick one, both are acceptable):
(a) add a bounded attempt budget to the dispatch loop: after N iterations (N small, e.g. 2 * number_of_connections + 2) stop and return the last error; or
(b) treat "refreshed, retried, and 401 again" as terminal for that connection: insert it into `excluded` on the second 401 so the loop advances to the next member.
Prefer (a) as a hard backstop even if you also do (b), because (b) alone does not cover a non-401 error class that also fails to advance the loop.

VERIFICATION (must go red first):
- A test that makes upstream return 401 and the refresh endpoint return a valid token, with ONE connection configured, and asserts the call terminates with an error within the budget instead of hanging.
- The test MUST have a timeout so a regression fails rather than hangs the suite forever.
- A test that a normal 401-then-refresh-then-success sequence still works (the healthy path must not regress).
close_reason: attempt_budget + refreshed_this_request; tests pin contract not failure (see commit msg)

title: P0 chat: the solo (non-combo) capacity-adapter fallback is missing entirely
description:
OpenProxy has no solo capacity-adapter fallback, so a PLAIN provider (not a combo) on a capacity adapter never falls back. 9router has it (.tmp/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js:143-158). This is the Direct arm, not the combo closure — a different code region from the combo-recursion fix, hence a separate bead.

VERIFY: a solo provider registered on a capacity adapter falls back to the next capacity when the first is exhausted; a solo provider NOT on an adapter is unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed in aac8b26e. The Direct arm called execute_single_model once with no chain, so a plain provider whose capacity was exhausted had nowhere to go, while the same provider inside a combo fell back to the adapter pool. The Direct arm now augments the single model with the capacity adapter and tries each candidate in turn, mirroring 9router chat.js:143-158. History stripping applies only to adapter-added models, never the one the client asked for. A provider not on an adapter yields a one-element chain and takes the old path. 2292 lib + 12 chat_completions pass; fmt/clippy clean. title: 1.2 - Format Detection & Translation Pipeline
description:
Format Detection & Translation Pipeline

## Scope
Detect API format from endpoint path + request body shape. Dispatch translation through typed registry.

## Subtasks
1. Format enum: OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, GeminiCli, OpenAIResponses, Vertex, Codex, Antigravity, Kiro, Cursor, Ollama, CommandCode
2. fn detect_format(endpoint, body_headers, body_json) -> Format — rules-based detection
3. Translator registry dispatching by (source, target) tuple
4. Translation pipeline: detect -> resolve -> translate (direct or pivot through OpenAI)
5. Response symmetry enforcement: every request translator MUST have matching response translator
6. Source format override via endpoint path (/v1/messages -> Claude, /v1/responses -> Responses)

## Detection Rules (fixed from 9router)
- /v1/responses -> OpenAI Responses
- /v1/messages -> Claude
- body.anthropic_version -> Claude (check BEFORE messages heuristics)
- body.contents[] -> Gemini/Antigravity
- User-Agent is HTTP HEADER not body field (9router bug: reads body.userAgent)
- model string with / does NOT exclude Claude (9router bug: body.model.includes("/") blocks it)

## Files
- src/format.rs — Format enum + detection
- src/translator/mod.rs — TranslatorRegistry, dispatch
- src/translator/registry.rs — Registry builder

## Tests
- /v1/messages with Claude body -> Claude
- /v1/responses -> OpenAIResponses
- /v1/chat/completions with messages[] + anthropic_version -> Claude (NOT OpenAI)
- Gemini contents[] -> Gemini
- Unknown defaults -> OpenAI

## 9router CRITICAL Bugs Fixed
- Pure-text Claude without body.system misclassified as OpenAI
- body.model.includes("/") blocks Claude detection for antigravity/claude-sonnet
- body.userAgent read as body field instead of HTTP header

title: P0: extract the stream EOF sequence so branch and yield order are testable
description:
THE FIX FOR THE FAILURE CLASS THIS EPIC KEEPT PRODUCING.

Six consecutive review rounds found the same shape of defect: the fix was correct AT THE FUNCTION and wrong AT THE CALL SITE. Concretely, in src/server/api/chat.rs:
  - a [DONE] sentinel gated on the provider but not on the branch taken, and emitted before the terminal flushes, silently truncating qoder and kiro streams
  - an allow-list copied literally from 9router, blocking kiro's application/vnd.amazon.eventstream — 9router has no binary provider, OpenProxy does
  - a saw_done flag declared, read, and never assigned, while the commit message described it as tracked
  - a terminal frame that kept its delimiter but skipped every other transform, the same 'last frame is special' oversight twice

Every unit test was GREEN through all of them, because they call the helper in isolation. src/server/api/chat.rs is large enough that no test reaches the stream generator.

THE FIX: pull the end-of-stream sequence out of the async_stream closure into a plain function that takes the branch it actually took plus the buffers and flush outputs, and RETURNS THE YIELDS IN ORDER. Signature roughly:

  fn finish_stream_eof(branch, provider, translate_buf, passthrough_buf, coalescer_frames, finish_frames) -> Vec<Emit>

so a test can assert the ORDER: a qoder request must emit its coalescer finish+usage chunk and not a [DONE]; a kiro request must emit its finish_stream terminal chunk and not a [DONE]; a real passthrough request must emit its last frame and then exactly one [DONE]; a passthrough whose upstream already sent [DONE] must emit none.

Also extract the per-chunk branch dispatch the same way, because the kiro P0 was a wrong branch PREDICATE at the dispatch site, not a wrong helper.

Scope: refactor only, no behaviour change beyond what the landed fixes already changed. Every landed fix (764469cd, db47e5f0, 08e746aa, 3ac819b3, 1c3d806f, e166b0bd, 3e9039e3) must keep passing, and the order assertions must fail if the sequence is reordered.
close_reason: EOF sequence extracted into plan_eof_emits so branch + yield ORDER is a unit-testable contract; 7 order tests. Also fixed a flaky 10s-sleep TTL test via the tokio clock domain. Commit 31bd4202.

title: P1 executor: retry budget off-by-one vs 9router, asymmetric URL rotation, and the refresh-resend ? that skips fallback
description:
Adjacent defects found 2026-09-25 while fixing the retry/status work in
openproxy-we9n (23e5698f). None is a live regression today — `fallback_urls`
is empty at every construction site, so N=1 in production — but each is wrong
against 9router and will go live the moment a fallback URL is wired.

(b) PRE-REFRESH STATUS RECORDED. default.rs records `status`, bound before the
    refresh resend; the resend's status is discarded and only `.is_success()`
    is read. A 401 whose post-refresh resend returns 429 is reported as 401.
    Low severity, but it is the wrong-error pattern, and it is the one case
    where the surfaced status misleads about why rotation failed.

(c) THE `?` ON THE REFRESH RESEND. default.rs still uses `?` for the resend
    send, so a transport error there propagates straight out of execute(),
    skipping the remaining fallback URLs and bypassing last_failure entirely.
    Pre-existing, but it means the "rotates to the next URL" claim only holds
    for the main send. One line: capture the Result and break into the loop.

(d) OFF-BY-ONE ON EVERY RETRYABLE BRANCH. 9router's `attempts` counts RETRIES
    (runtimeConfig.js:78-83), so budget 3 means 4 fetches per URL. The Rust
    `max_attempts = 3` with `retry + 1 < max_attempts` guards means 3 total.
    We are conservative — fewer requests than 9router — but it is a
    divergence in the total-attempt count, which is the thing most likely to be
    wrong.

(e) 502/503 RETRY ONLY ON THE LAST URL, 504 ON EVERY URL. The 502 and 503
    branches guard on `url == urls.last().unwrap()`; the 504 branch has no such
    guard. A 502 on url 0 returns raw after one send while a 504 on url 0 burns
    two and rotates. 9router's tryRetry has no such asymmetry (base.js:155).

VERIFY: a provider configured with two fallback URLs retries each URL to the
documented budget, rotates between them, and reports the final real status.
close_reason: All four fixed. (d) OFF-BY-ONE: 9router's budget counts RETRIES, not total attempts - tryRetry increments retryAttemptsByUrl and returns true while below the configured attempts (base.js:113), so budget 3 is four fetches. We looped three times total, so every retryable status was one fetch short. The numbers in retry_policy already matched DEFAULT_RETRY_CONFIG exactly; only the interpretation differed. The loop bound is now sourced from retry_policy so the two cannot drift. (e) 502/503 only retried on the LAST fallback URL while 504 retried on every URL; tryRetry is per-URL and never gated on being last. Both guards removed. (c) The refreshed-credential resend used '?', so a transport failure there propagated straight out of execute(), skipping every remaining fallback URL and bypassing last_failure - a DNS blip on the resend abandoned a chain the main send would have rotated through. It now records the failure and breaks into the loop. (b) The resend's status is now recorded; status was bound before the refresh and never updated, so a 401 whose resend answered 429 was reported as 401, and the caller picks cooldown/backoff from that number. 468 lib executor + 51 executor_pool_behavior pass; fmt/clippy clean. NOTE this raises the worst-case fetch count per URL from 3 to 4, which is the parity-correct value but IS more upstream traffic on a hard-failing provider - N=1 in production today since fallback_urls is empty at every construction site.

title: P3: Background model-catalog sync from models.dev
description:
9router 0532f00d (feat(models): refresh model capabilities from models.dev in the background) + e6f5724b (fix(models): stop the catalog sync from erasing its own output) + d0172455 (fix(models): drop the worker thread from the catalog sync) introduced (and fixed bugs in) a background job that periodically refreshes model capability metadata from the external models.dev registry. Rust catalog (provider_catalog.json / 9router.json) is static/JSON-only — no background sync job.

Lower priority: data-freshness convenience, not correctness/security — but stale capability metadata (context windows, modalities, pricing) drifts silently without it.

Steps:
1. git show all three commits: models.dev API shape polled, merge strategy (must NOT overwrite locally-curated fields — exactly the e6f5724b bug, so design the Rust merge to avoid it from the start), and why the worker-thread approach was dropped in d0172455 (favor whatever async-task model 9router settled on, e.g. plain async interval task, not a dedicated OS thread).
2. Implement as a background async task in server startup where other periodic jobs live; atomic write, never truncate-then-write (avoid partial-catalog corruption on crash).

Acceptance: merge preserves manually-set fields models.dev lacks; updates fields it provides; failed/malformed response leaves catalog intact. Unit tests added.

title: P0 streaming: per-frame usage extraction with field-wise max merge
description:
On an Anthropic stream the LAST raw frame is message_stop (no usage) or message_delta (output only), so prompt tokens and both cache counters are structurally unreachable. record_streaming_usage reads only that last frame
(src/server/api/chat.rs, last_data = Some(chunk.clone()) per chunk).

9router runs extractUsage on EVERY chunk and folds it with a field-wise max
merge, precisely because 'Anthropic splits usage across events: message_start
has real input+cache, message_delta has the real cumulative output'
(.tmp/9router/open-sse/utils/stream.js:319-321, :197-199).

Consequence: the ledger records tokens: null / cost 0.00 for EVERY Claude
streaming request — the dominant mode for Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, OpenClaw.
That $0 flows into monthly_spend_for_key, so the per-key monthly_budget_usd
kill-switch never sees streaming spend at all. strip_sse_data_prefix also keeps
only the first line, so a multi-frame or split frame returns None outright.

FIX: run the extractor on every data: frame in BOTH stream arms, fold into a
running Option<TokenUsage> with a field-wise max merge, and pass the accumulator
to record_streaming_usage. Keep the existing estimator only as a fallback when
no frame yielded usage.

VERIFY: a synthetic Anthropic stream (message_start carrying input_tokens and
cache_creation_input_tokens, message_delta carrying output_tokens, message_stop
carrying none) must record all three, with cache counters preserved. Add the
negative case: a stream where the only usage is in a NON-final frame still
records it — that is the whole regression.
close_reason:
Implemented in two commits, both pushed.

7c553c85 merged per-frame usage with a field-wise max in both stream arms.
38b5fe2a (and the follow-up) fixed the extractor itself, which the bead review
showed made the merge a NO-OP for Claude: strip_sse_data_prefix took line 0,
which on an Anthropic frame is 'event: ...' and never 'data: ...'; and the
Anthropic message_start shape nests usage under message.usage, which the
extractor did not read at all.

Net effect now live: a Claude stream that previously recorded tokens:null /
cost 0.00 (so the monthly_budget_usd kill-switch never saw streaming spend)
records input tokens, output tokens and both cache counters.

The REVIEW also found the original merge tests could not have failed, because
they fed merge_token_usage pre-built TokenUsage instead of running real frames
through the extractor. Replaced with tests that run real Anthropic frame bytes
through extract-then-merge.

Remaining framing work is tracked separately as openproxy-0ph4.

title: P0 oauth: device-code flow transitions and connect paths
description:
P0 oauth: the dashboard cannot connect ANY non-kiro device-code provider, and three OAuth providers can never be probed.

VERIFIED 2026-09-25 against this tree by direct source read. 9router is
canonical.

REMOVED: the audit's "finding 3" (device-code START transition) was a DUPLICATE
of finding 1. Both name oauth.rs:2945, the same route (oauth.rs:6649), and the
same fix. There is no second guard anywhere — grep for `device-code` in src/
returns only that one registration.

--- FINDING 1 — the dashboard OAuth modal cannot connect any non-kiro device-code provider (CONFIRMED) ---
GAP: the first statement of start_device_code_compat (oauth.rs:2945) is
`if provider != "kiro" { return 400 "Provider does not support device code flow" }`.
The route is bound at oauth.rs:6648-6651 as
GET /api/oauth/{provider}/device-code. The dashboard modal
(web/src/shared/components/OAuthModal.tsx:195-220) sends all 11 device-code
providers down that GET. Net: 10 of them — github, qwen, kimi, kimi-coding,
kilocode, codebuddy, codebuddy-cn, qoder, grok-cli, kimchi — get an instant 400.
A working multi-provider implementation ALREADY EXISTS at oauth.rs:4756-4873
(start_device_code, gated by is_device_code_provider at oauth.rs:689-704) but is
bound to the underscore route POST /api/oauth/{provider}/device_code
(oauth.rs:6652), which the dashboard never calls.
FAILURE: Connect on GitHub / Kimi / KiloCode / Qoder / Grok-CLI / CodeBuddy* /
Qwen / Kimchi returns HTTP 400 and the modal throws into its error step
(OAuthModal.tsx:222). The user can never authenticate those providers.
FIX: route the dashboard to the working endpoint, or replace the kiro-only guard
with a registry-driven is_device_code_provider check.

NOTE: the audit's proposed `flowType` lookup is 9router's schema and does not
exist here — OAuthProviderConfig (src/oauth/providers.rs:43-52) has no such
field. The Rust equivalent is is_device_code_provider (oauth.rs:689).

--- FINDING 2 — the poll transition is unreachable; casing is only one of two blockers (CONFIRMED) ---
GAP: the poll handler requires snake_case `device_code` (oauth.rs:4925) and 400s
with missing_device_code otherwise. The dashboard sends camelCase
(OAuthModal.tsx:153-157 sends { deviceCode, codeVerifier, extraData }).
camelCase is honoured ONLY for kiro, via KiroCompatPollBody (oauth.rs:482-490) —
already `#[serde(rename_all="camelCase")]` with
`#[serde(alias="device_code")]`, i.e. exactly the struct the audit proposed, but
kiro-scoped. The CLI does send snake_case (src/cli/provider_oauth.rs:128), which
is why tests/oauth_kiro_device_code_api.rs:238-252 passes and hid this.
SECOND BLOCKER THE AUDIT MISSED: for non-kiro providers oauth.rs:4919-4922 calls
require_api_key_with_reload BEFORE the field lookup, and the modal sends no auth
header — so the poll fails 401 before the casing check is ever reached. Fixing
casing alone is therefore NOT sufficient; the pending→authorized transition stays
unreachable for every non-kiro device-code provider from the dashboard.
FIX: accept both spellings on the general path, and reconcile the auth
requirement with what the modal actually sends (or have the modal send a key).

--- FINDING 3 — grok-cli, qoder and kimchi OAuth connections always test as errors (CONFIRMED) ---
GAP: oauth_probe_request (src/server/api/provider_connection_test.rs:1609-1687)
has arms for codex, gemini-cli/antigravity, github, iflow, kilocode, gitlab, and
`_ => None` (1686). None becomes invalid("Provider test not supported") at :356,
and providers.rs:169-171 then persists test_status "error" plus last_error.
Verified these three are not short-circuited earlier: they are absent from
is_refreshable_provider (1967), is_check_expiry_provider (1974), the
cursor||codebuddy early-valid branch (266), and the cline branch (275). OAuth
connections are stored with auth_type "oauth" (oauth.rs:1453), so :138-143 routes
them to test_oauth_connection.
FAILURE: POST /api/providers/{id}/test on a connected grok-cli / qoder / kimchi
OAuth connection always returns {valid:false, "Provider test not supported"} and
writes testStatus:"error", regardless of whether the token is actually valid.
FIX: add the three arms to oauth_probe_request.

TWO ADJACENT GAPS THE AUDIT MISSED: grok-cli is listed in
is_device_code_provider (oauth.rs:701) but has no providers::get_config arm
(src/oauth/providers.rs:539-566), so the working device-code path 400s it as
"Unknown provider"; and kimchi is in neither list although the modal treats it
as device-code (its config is browser_token, providers.rs:245-246).

--- COMPLETION RULE ---
Three findings, all verified CONFIRMED. If you believe one is already fixed,
PROVE it — name the guard or the commit — before deleting it.
Verification: cargo test -p openproxy --lib oauth, plus a case that starts and
polls a non-kiro device-code provider exactly the way OAuthModal.tsx does
(camelCase body, no auth header) and asserts pending→authorized is reachable.
notes:
FINDING 3 NOT DONE — needs an endpoint decision, deliberately not guessed.

The defect is real and unchanged: oauth_probe_request
(src/server/api/provider_connection_test.rs:1609-1687) has arms for codex,
gemini-cli/antigravity, github, iflow, kilocode, gitlab, and `_ => None`
(1686). None becomes invalid("Provider test not supported") at :356, and
providers.rs:169-171 persists test_status "error" + last_error. So grok-cli,
qoder and kimchi OAuth connections always report an error regardless of
whether the token is valid.

WHY IT WAS NOT JUST WRITTEN: the probe URL is not the same on both sides, and
guessing it would invert the bug this finding is about — a wrong URL marks a
VALID connection as error, which is the exact failure being fixed.

  - qoder. 9router probes https://openapi.qoder.sh/api/v1/userinfo (registry
    qoder.js:52; the -cn variant uses openapi.qoder.com.cn). OpenProxy's own
    config (src/oauth/providers.rs:306-307) points at https://api.qoder.ai/ —
    a different host. Which one answers a userinfo call is unverified.
  - grok-cli. 9router probes ${GROK_CLI_BASE_URL}/user =
    https://cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/user with x-xai-token-auth:
    xai-grok-cli and x-grok-client-identifier headers
    (registry/grok-cli.js:48,61; config/grokCli.js:3; services/grokCliModels.js:61).
    OpenProxy has NO grok-cli entry in the OAuth provider registry at all —
    it is listed in is_device_code_provider (oauth.rs:701) but get_config has
    no arm, so the device-code start 400s it as "Unknown provider". There is no
    base URL to probe against until that gap is closed.
  - kimchi. OpenProxy already defines validation_url
    https://api.cast.ai/v1/llm/openai/supported-providers in its config
    (src/oauth/providers.rs:252-254); 9router separately lists userInfoUrl
    https://app.kimchi.dev/api/v1/me (registry/kimchi.js:45). kimchi is also a
    browser_token flow, not device-code, so it is absent from
    is_device_code_provider even though the modal treats it as device-code.

TO FINISH: confirm the reachable userinfo endpoint per provider (ideally by
calling it), then add the three arms following the kilocode/gitlab shape. For
grok-cli that means adding the registry entry first. Add a test per arm that
asserts a 200 probe is reported valid — the negative case already exists by
default, which is why this went unnoticed.
close_reason: All three findings now fixed. F1 and F2 in 85bde31f/3d3fb181 (device-code start reachable for 9 of 11 providers, poll accepting both casings and a session or a key, with the snapshot reload kept). F3 in this commit: grok-cli, qoder and kimchi had no oauth_probe_request arm, so every test of one returned 'Provider test not supported' and persisted testStatus 'error' regardless of the token. Endpoints are sourced from the providers' own executors rather than 9router's registry, which disagrees - 9router lists openapi.qoder.sh while the executor dials api2/api3.qoder.sh by token prefix, and OpenProxy has no userInfoUrl equivalent. QoderExecutor::inference_base was made public so the probe reuses the host choice instead of re-deriving logic that drifts. Two tests, both proven to fail with the arms removed. STILL OPEN from this bead's own text: grok-cli is listed in is_device_code_provider but has no OAuthProviderConfig in the registry, so the device-code start 400s it as 'Unknown provider'; and the dashboard modal offers kimchi while the backend allowlists codebuddy-intl, which the modal does not offer. Those are a registry-entry question and a modal/allowlist mismatch, not parity gaps, and want their own bead.

title: P0: Qoder billing block detection — first-frame peek → 403
description:
Qoder executor needs first-frame billing block detection. 9router v0.5.55 adds peekFirstQoderFrame() that reads the first SSE frame before piping. If it contains billing/quota error (codes 112, 10605, or pricingUrl), return 403 JSON to trigger combo/account fallback. Currently the qoder executor (src/core/executor/qoder.rs) has no such detection — billing errors leak into chat response text.

## Reference
- .tmp/9router/open-sse/executors/qoder.js — isBillingBlock(), peekFirstQoderFrame()
- Codes: 112 (quota exhausted), 10605 (queue throttle), pricingUrl field

## Implementation
1. Add peek_first_qoder_frame() that reads first SSE event from the stream
2. Parse JSON payload, check for billing error codes
3. If billing block detected, return error response (403) without piping
4. If clean, re-process peeked bytes into normal SSE stream
5. Test: mock billing error response → verify 403 returned
6. Test: mock normal response → verify peeked bytes are not lost

title: P0: four CLI-tool config write paths destroy the user's file on a JSON parse error
description:
P0: four CLI-tool config write paths silently destroy the user's file on a JSON parse error.

NEW FINDING 2026-09-25 — not present in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md.
Found while verifying openproxy-mljv, which claimed a different (and refuted)
OpenClaw defect. Independently reproduced by reading the call sites.

THE DEFECT: src/server/api/cli_tools.rs:1958 defines

    fn parse_json_object_or_default(content: &str) -> serde_json::Map<String, Value> {
        match serde_json::from_str::<Value>(content) {
            Ok(Value::Object(object)) => object,
            _ => serde_json::Map::new(),          // <-- swallows the parse error
        }
    }

Four write paths pair this with `fs::read_to_string` and then write the map
back, so ANY parse failure on the user's existing file produces an empty map,
the mutation adds only the one path being written, and the whole file is
overwritten with essentially nothing:

    write_droid_settings        cli_tools.rs:1331
    reset_droid_settings        cli_tools.rs:1411
    write_openclaw_settings     cli_tools.rs:1707
    write_openclaw_agent_models cli_tools.rs:1908

FAILURE: the user's openclaw.json contains a trailing comma, a comment, a BOM,
or was truncated by an unclean shutdown. The user changes one model in the
OpenProxy dashboard and saves. Every other key in their file is gone. There is
no error, no warning, and no backup — the response is a normal 200.

SCOPE — the same pattern elsewhere is SAFE and must not be "fixed":
src/server/api/cli_tools.rs:1943 read_json_optional does
`Ok(Some(serde_json::from_str(&content)?))` — the `?` propagates, so
write_claude_settings (claude_settings.rs:207), write_skip_approvals
(cowork_settings.rs:424) and bootstrap_deployment_mode (cowork_settings.rs:701)
abort on malformed input instead of overwriting. Their `_ => Map::new()` arm is
only reachable for valid-JSON-that-is-not-an-object, which is a far weaker edge
and is NOT data loss. src/db/sqlite/import.rs:230 is not a write path.
src/server/api/cli_tools/droid_settings.rs:291 is a byte-identical duplicate of
the parser and should be deduplicated in the same change.

WHY IT SURVIVED THE EARLIER FIX: the opencode.jsonc wipe-config bug was already
fixed — src/server/api/cli_tools.rs has read_opencode_jsonc / blank_jsonc_noise
/ serialize_jsonc wired to the opencode card. The same tolerance was never
applied to openclaw or droid, which is why the class looked closed.

FIX: in the four write paths, distinguish "file absent" from "file present but
unparseable". Absent -> start from an empty map (current behaviour is right).
Present-but-unparseable -> return an error and write nothing. Use the existing
parse_json_object_required (cli_tools.rs:1966) for the present case, or add a
Result-returning sibling. Deduplicate the parser while you are in there.

VERIFY: for each of the four paths, seed the target file with invalid JSON
(trailing comma is enough), invoke the write endpoint, assert (a) the response
is an error, and (b) the file on disk is byte-identical to the seed. Add the
positive case too: a valid file with unrelated keys survives a write that
touches one key. Assert on bytes, not on parsed content — the failure mode is
precisely that the file still parses after being emptied.
notes: SCOPE CORRECTED after peer review. The first commit (cceddcf2) closed 4 live paths but the title overclaimed; follow-ups 69a6ce1a closed codex auth.json (the worst case - it held OAuth tokens and losing the refresh_token silently switched the CLI to apikey auth), codex config.toml, the copilot ARRAY twin, cowork's read_json_optional, and the unconditional cowork bytes[i] as char UTF-8 corruption. Nine tests now cover it. The droid_settings submodule is DEAD - not declared anywhere, never compiled - so the earlier '6 paths' count was 4 live. Deferred by user decision, filed separately.
close_reason: Complete. The first commit closed 4 live write paths; a peer sweep found the title was overclaiming and found 5 more, all now fixed in 116b9b16: codex auth.json (the sharpest - it holds OAuth tokens, so a swallowed parse error discarded the refresh_token and silently switched the CLI to apikey auth), codex config.toml, the copilot ARRAY twin (top-level array, so the object-shaped helper could never reach it), cowork's read_json_optional (present-but-unparseable read as absent), and cowork's unconditional bytes[i] as char UTF-8 corruption that damaged any WELL-FORMED config with non-ASCII. 6 HTTP tests in cli_tools_config_preservation plus 4 unit tests in cowork_settings, including the codex one asserting a fake refresh_token survives. The dead droid_settings submodule is untouched and documented as dead in the test header. Related class filed separately as openproxy-jpjg and the web-side transports as openproxy-st40.

title: P0 streaming: align the non-SSE guard with 9router
description:
The non-SSE guard is a 3-type deny-list returning a hardcoded 502, where 9router pipes the body. Verified consequences:
 (a) A 2xx application/json from a provider that ignored stream:true becomes a 502. 502 is RETRYABLE for multi-provider clients, so one flaky provider triggers a retry storm — this is the highest-traffic of the three.
 (b) An unlisted non-SSE type is piped straight into the SSE transform, yielding garbage frames with no terminal [DONE] — the hang the guard exists to prevent.
 (c) Raw upstream HTML is echoed into error.message. That is exactly the XSS surface 9router's own comment says the title-clamp exists to block.
Note the verifier established 9router's '|| 502' is dead code on this path (non-2xx returns earlier), so the real delta is 200-with-error-body vs 502, not 5xx propagation. Scope accordingly.

DEPENDS ON: openproxy-0ph4 (SSE frame-boundary de-framing) (the de-framed type is what this guard classifies). Evidence in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'non-SSE').

FIX: replace the deny-list with 9router's allow-list rule, pass the upstream status through rather than rewriting it, and never echo raw upstream bytes into an error message.

VERIFY: a 200-with-JSON-body produces a well-formed client response, not a 502; an unlisted content type produces an explicit error, not garbage frames; an HTML error body is not reflected verbatim into any field the client renders.
close_reason: 9router non-SSE guard: allow-list + upstream status passthrough + <title> extraction (XSS sink). Commits 08e746aa, 3ac819b3 (kiro P0 from the literal port).

title: 2.2 - Token Refresh & OAuth
description:
Token Refresh & OAuth

## Scope
Per-provider OAuth token refresh with retry, dedup, and edge case handling.

## Subtasks
1. Refresh dispatch table: provider -> refresh function
2. Jittered exponential backoff retry (not linear: 9router uses 1s/2s/3s with no jitter)
3. Refresh dedup: cache IN-FLIGHT Promise, not null result (9router: caches null for 10s, defeats retry)
4. Unrecoverable error detection: invalid_grant, refresh_token_reused -> STOP retry immediately
5. Vertex JWT minting with in-memory cache + TTL (thread-safe, atomic read+write)
6. getAllAccessTokens passes ALL connection fields including providerSpecificData (9router: drops it, breaks Kiro)

## 9router CRITICAL Fixes
- dedup caches null for 10s: executor.refreshCredentials returns null on network error, cached. Fix: only cache SUCCESS.
- Object.assign race on credentials: concurrent 401 requests race on same object. Fix: clone-then-swap.
- getAllAccessTokens drops providerSpecificData: Kiro needs clientId/secret/region. Fix: pass all fields.
- vertex unreachable via getAccessToken: guard checks refreshToken string type, vertex uses apiKey. Fix: per-provider guard.
- vertexTokenCache not thread-safe: concurrent minting overwrites each other. Fix: tokio::sync::RwLock.

## Files
- src/auth/refresh.rs — Refresh dispatcher + per-provider implementations
- src/auth/dedup.rs — Concurrent refresh deduplication
- src/auth/vertex.rs — Vertex JWT minting with cache

## Tests
- Successful refresh returns new tokens
- Null result NOT cached (retries work)
- Unrecoverable error stops retry
- Concurrent refresh returns same result
- Vertex cache doesn't double-mint

     GET /v1/models/{kind} both omit disabled ids, reading the SAME disabled-map

     source is what caused this divergence; do not introduce a second one.

     response shape.

extractor, so '?kind=' is silently ignored by axum and asserting it would tempt
an implementer to invent a phantom parameter):

title: P1 provider parity (tail): per-provider header, discovery and transform divergences
description:
PART OF A SPLIT, re-filed by polish round 3 — the original area clustering mis-binned findings by subsystem. CHECK THE WORKING TREE FIRST: several predate fixes that have since landed, and some were duplicates of a sibling bead's item, now removed.

COMPLETION RULE: this is a WORK LIST. Every finding is confirmed and in scope. If you believe one is unreachable, PROVE it by naming the guard and delete the finding. 'Low value' is not a reason.

9router is canonical, including its quirks, unless the finding says the quirk is the defect. Evidence for every finding is in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md — search by the location below.

--- FINDINGS ---
1. [P1] Claude-family identity headers sent to api.anthropic.com
   GAP: OpenProxy's claude provider has no static Claude-CLI fingerprint; those identity headers appear only after a Claude Code client request has warmed a global cache — a mechanism 9Router does not have at all.
2. [P1] Client request headers reaching provider executors
   GAP: OpenProxy drops the client header map at the executor boundary: `raw_headers` is hardcoded empty for opencode/opencode-go, and cursor reads a `provider_specific_data.rawHeaders` key that is never populated.
3. [P1] OpenProxy `src/core/rtk/mod.rs:213-227`, `src/core/translator/ponytail.rs:131-146`, `src/core/rtk/system_inject.rs:16-22`
   GAP: OpenProxy has no Kiro branch in the system-prompt injector, so caveman, ponytail and the global system-prompt override are all no-ops on `kr/` models.
4. [P1] OpenProxy `src/server/api/mod.rs` (`UpdateSettingsRequest`) vs `web/src/components/cli-tools/ClaudeToolCard.tsx:179`
   GAP: `ccFilterNaming` is a live toggle on the Claude CLI-tool card in both products, but OpenProxy's fixed-allowlist settings PATCH silently discards it, so the bypass it controls is permanently disabled.
5. [P1] POST /api/providers/{id}/test — codex 400 acceptance
   GAP: OpenProxy adds a body-content predicate to codex's 400 acceptance that 9router does not have.
6. [P1] POST /api/providers/{id}/test — codex probe identity headers
   GAP: OpenProxy sends a different CLI identity User-Agent and an extra `session_id` header on the codex probe.
7. [P1] Zed login — `provider_specific_data` contract
   GAP: The Zed login persists neither `systemId` nor `organizationId` into provider_specific_data, so the system-id header is never sent and the organization must be rediscovered on every single request.
8. [P1] Zed organization-id resolution (`resolveZedOrganizationId` equivalent)
   GAP: The two resolvers read disjoint field sets: every key 9router reads (`defaultOrganizationId`, `default_organization_id`, `organizations[].id`) is ignored by OpenProxy, and every key OpenProxy reads (`organization.id`, bare `organization_id`
9. [P1] forceStream provider set — opencode / oc

title: P1 resilience: the SSE stall watchdog is 180s per-chunk against 9router's 360s
description:
SSE_STALL_TIMEOUT (src/server/api/chat.rs:110) is 180s, applied PER CHUNK to response.bytes_stream() at :3852 and :4012. 9router's STR_* default is 360s. A provider that pauses between chunks for longer than 180s but less than 360s is cut off by OpenProxy and not by 9router.

Split out of the old bead: this is a constant, not the retry work. Also note runtime_config.rs:44 carries a 360s value that is DEAD CODE — the bead must say whether to wire it or delete it, not 'align' it, because wiring it silently changes a third clock nobody audited.

VERIFY: a provider whose inter-chunk gap is 200s completes on OpenProxy after this change, and a gap beyond the aligned budget still terminates the stream rather than hanging.
close_reason: SSE stall clock 180s -> 360s, sourced from runtime_config::STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS which had 360s and zero readers. Commit d4663d5f.

title: 3.1 - Base Executor Trait & HTTP Client
description: trait ProviderExecutor with async execute. Common HTTP: URL building, headers, retry per status. Proxy-aware fetch: env proxy, connection proxy, Vercel relay. AbortSignal integration. Connection vs stream stall timeout. Files: src/executor/trait.rs, src/executor/http.rs, src/executor/retry.rs. 9router fixes: ProxyAgent leak on concurrent init, global fetch patching, Headers spread on Headers object loses headers.

title: RTK streaming-side transforms (mod/autodetect/headroom)
description:
PART OF A SPLIT, re-filed by polish round 3 — the original area clustering mis-binned findings by subsystem. CHECK THE WORKING TREE FIRST: several predate fixes that have since landed, and some were duplicates of a sibling bead's item, now removed.

COMPLETION RULE: this is a WORK LIST. Every finding is confirmed and in scope. If you believe one is unreachable, PROVE it by naming the guard and delete the finding. 'Low value' is not a reason.

9router is canonical, including its quirks, unless the finding says the quirk is the defect. Evidence for every finding is in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md — search by the location below.

--- FINDINGS ---
1. [P1] open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:278-281 vs src/core/rtk/mod.rs:139-148 (+ 209-211, 524-528)
   GAP: OpenProxy only injects the Caveman system prompt when the request already exceeds 512-2048 estimated tokens; 9Router injects it on every request once enabled.
2. [P1] open-sse/rtk/filters/grep.js:13 vs src/core/rtk/filters/mod.rs:404-407
   GAP: OpenProxy's grep filter is a no-op: the second-colon search can never succeed, so no line is ever matched and grep_impl always returns the input verbatim.
3. [P1] open-sse/rtk/systemInject.js:164-172 vs src/core/rtk/mod.rs:246-258 (and src/core/translator/ponytail.rs:189-204)
   GAP: For a Responses-API body with an `input` array, OpenProxy injects `{role:"system", content:"<string>"}` — an input item with no `type` and non-array content — instead of 9Router's typed `{type:"message", role:"system", content:[{type:"input
4. [P1] open-sse/rtk/systemInject.js:17-19 and :273-292 vs src/core/rtk/mod.rs:213-228
   GAP: OpenProxy has no Kiro arm at all — a conversationState body falls through every branch and the prompt is silently dropped.
5. [P2] open-sse/rtk/index.js:18-21 vs src/core/rtk/mod.rs:596-601 + :721-726
   GAP: When `messages` exists but is not an array while `input` is, OpenProxy compressed `input` and then wrote it into `messages`, clobbering the original field.
6. [P2] open-sse/rtk/index.js:26-27 and :64-67 vs src/core/rtk/mod.rs:596-601 + :611 + :673
   GAP: One non-object element in messages/content aborts OpenProxy's entire RTK pass and leaves the body untouched; 9Router skips that element and compresses the rest.
7. [P3] open-sse/rtk/systemInject.js:75-79 and :223 vs src/core/rtk/mod.rs:400-413 and :299-305
   GAP: Prompt-injection idempotency is substring-based in OpenProxy but exact-segment-based in 9Router, so an existing system prompt that merely mentions the injection text suppresses re-injection in OpenProxy only.
8. [P1] open-sse/rtk/autodetect.js:84-94 vs src/core/rtk/autodetect.rs:222-231
   GAP: Windows drive-letter paths are never path-like in OpenProxy, so the `non_empty.every(isPathLike)` find-detection can never fire for Windows find output.
9. [P2] open-sse/rtk/autodetect.js:28-71 vs src/core/rtk/autodetect.rs:95-103 + :163-190
   GAP: OpenProxy routes three whole classes of tool output (test-runner logs, large JSON/NDJSON blobs, tabular data) to filters that do not exist in 9Router, changing the compressed payload for those inputs.
10. [P2] open-sse/rtk/autodetect.js:41 + :61 vs src/core/rtk/autodetect.rs:155-156 + :242-256
   GAP: The read-numbered activation threshold counts lines in the whole body in OpenProxy but only within the 1024-char detection window in 9Router, so any long numbered file dump selects a different filter.
11. [P1] open-sse/rtk/headroom.js:162-167 vs src/core/rtk/headroom.rs:590-694
   GAP: OpenProxy's Kiro Headroom projection ignores conversationState.currentMessage and returns None outright when history is missing/empty, so the newest turn — where the tool-result bloat lives — is never compressed.
12. [P2] open-sse/rtk/headroom.js:65-77 vs src/core/rtk/headroom.rs:370 + :890-892
   GAP: OpenProxy's /v1/compress endpoint drops the URL query string, so a Headroom URL that carries an auth token or tenant selector in the query is called without it.
