title: P0: fusion strategy ignores disabledModels + quarantine; test-model reports 400 as success
description:
P0. Core surface #3. Confirmed by two verification lenses. User-visible promise is broken and money is involved.

THE DEFECT: the Fusion strategy ignores the disabled-members list and the quarantine map, so muted members are still dispatched to — and still billed.

  src/server/api/chat.rs:453  computes `disabled_members`
  src/server/api/chat.rs:459  computes the capacity-augmented list
  both reach ONLY the non-fusion branch at :653-657
  the fusion branch at :500 passes raw `&combo_models` to handle_fusion_chat_deferred (:518-521) / handle_fusion_chat (:558-561)
  handle_fusion_chat_inner (src/core/combo/fusion.rs:587) fans out to EVERY panel with no skip set
  quarantine is likewise only marked in the non-fusion closure (:739-747)

The UI contract is explicit and the user relies on it:
  - mute tooltip "Disable — keep in list but never dispatch to it" (ComboFormModal.tsx:215-234)
  - card renders the member struck through as "Disabled — never dispatched" (CombosPageClient.tsx:420-432)
  - the amber "cooling down" pill / "Clear cooldowns" (ComboFormModal.tsx:185-193, 466-476) reads /api/combos/{id}/health -> combo_quarantine_for (src/server/api/admin_items.rs:570) — a map the fusion path never writes.

REPRO: combo "f" = [unconfigured openai, working anthropic], strategy = Fusion. Mute the openai member, save. The panel still dispatches to it on every request; no quarantine entry is ever created.

THE FIX: build `fusion_panels` = combo_models MINUS disabled_members MINUS combo_quarantine_for(name) (src/core/combo/mod.rs:691 — the PUBLIC accessor, not the private quarantined_members) MINUS core::health::is_model_degraded. Pass that instead of `&combo_models` at both call sites, and use its length for panel_count so min_panel clamping stays correct. When it empties, return the same 400/503 the non-fusion path uses (mod.rs:868-887) instead of fanning out to nothing. Mark quarantine in the fusion error arm too.

SECOND FIX IN THIS BEAD (same root: a UI that says OK when the request would fail):
  src/server/api/provider_model_tests.rs:297 and :198  `let ok = status == OK || status == BAD_REQUEST;` -> error: None
  The 400 is openproxy's OWN in-process rejection — chat.rs:1426-1430 returns ComboAttemptError{400,"No credentials for provider: X"} when no connection is selectable, which is exactly the unconfigured-provider and providers-page-disabled-model case. ComboFormModal.tsx:327-334 maps ok -> "ok" and :165-173 renders a green check.
  The sibling endpoint already does it right: src/server/api/providers.rs:432 uses response.status().is_success().
  FIX: drop the `|| BAD_REQUEST` clause at both sites and parse the body so the operator sees "No credentials for provider: X" instead of a tick.

VERIFICATION (must go red first):
 - Mute a member of a Fusion combo, dispatch, assert the panel set excludes it (assert on what the panel executor received, not on a log line).
 - A test that a faulted/quarantined member is excluded from the next Fusion dispatch.
 - A test that an unconfigured member returns ok:false from the test endpoint — mirror the existing assertion style at tests/providers_api.rs:774-781.
close_reason: fusion_panels excludes disabled/quarantined/degraded; 400-as-success fixed

title: P0 resilience: retry network errors and 5xx in the DefaultExecutor send loop
description:
Network failures, connection refused, TLS errors and client timeouts get ZERO retries in the DefaultExecutor path and surface as terminal errors. Separately, 502/503 from a NON-FINAL url bypass the retry path.

Split out of the old bead because this is a one-file, self-contained P0 that should not be blocked behind two timeout changes in a different subsystem.

IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT (bead review): src/core/executor/default.rs:565 with_fallback is #[allow(dead_code)] with zero callers, and :532 / :541 / :953 all set fallback_urls: Vec::new(), so the per-URL retry PLACEMENT fix is UNVERIFIABLE until fallback_urls is actually wired. This bead therefore covers the SAME-URL 502/503/504 retry counts. The placement fix needs a separate bead that first wires fallback_urls, and that bead must say so — otherwise an implementer will write a test that passes because there is only ever one URL.

EVIDENCE: docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'retry').

VERIFY: wiremock failing the first N attempts on the SAME url then succeeding must succeed within 9router's budget; a terminal connection-refused must be retried per 9router's count and then surface the LAST error, not the first.
close_reason: Network errors now retry on the 502 budget per 9router, one shared counter. Commits 3e9039e3, 376ba4cd.

title: P0 dashboard: gate /dashboard/* behind a session check
description:
OpenProxy serves the full dashboard HTML shell for ANY unauthenticated /dashboard/* deep link. Verified scope: this is dashboard NAVIGATION only — the handler is a Router::fallback and is_rust_owned_path hard-404s /api, /v1 and /codex, so NO client request path is affected. Crawlers, link checkers and uptime monitors see 200 for deleted or renamed routes, so route regressions are undetectable, and a user following a stale link lands on a plausible-looking but wrong screen with no not-found signal.

Split out of the old bead because it shares no code with the Shutdown button problem: this needs new middleware in the dashboard shell (src/server/dashboard/mod.rs:45-63, dashboard_fallback), not a new API route.

VERIFIED 2026-09-25: no guard exists today. src/lib.rs:41-42 merges
`server::api::routes(state)` with `server::dashboard::routes()` and layers only
real_ip_middleware and cors (lib.rs:45-46). dashboard/mod.rs:41-43 is a bare
`Router::new().fallback(dashboard_fallback)`, and serve_embedded
(dashboard/mod.rs:80-125) returns the SPA shell for any /dashboard/* path.
No `dashboard_auth_middleware` exists anywhere in src/.

ADDED 2026-09-25 — the tunnel/tailscale host gate, which the original scope
missed. This is a genuinely uncovered increment, not a duplicate: no host-based
guard exists at all today. src/server/guard.rs provides only
real_ip_middleware, require_protected, require_admin and require_local_only —
there is no tunnel/tailscale host check, so the dashboard shell is served
regardless of how the request reached the host. A deployment exposed via tunnel
or tailscale serves the full dashboard shell with no host gate applied.

FIX:
1. Add a requireLogin session check to the /dashboard/* shell, with the same
   carve-outs the handler already has. Keep the public pages (login, callback,
   landing) open, or onboarding breaks.
2. Apply the tunnel/tailscale host gate to the same middleware, so a request
   arriving over a tunnel/tailscale host is evaluated against the same rules
   the API surface uses rather than falling through the dashboard fallback

title: Chat/translator: global model(level) stripThinkingSuffix + budget parity
description:
# Translator/chat: global stripThinkingSuffix model(level) + budget map parity

## Background
9router `thinkingUnified.js`: `stripThinkingSuffix` for `model(high|medium|low|…)` style, capture/apply thinking across formats, LEVEL_TO_BUDGET (low=1024, high=24576, …).

OpenProxy today:
- Kiro: `kiro_constants::strip_thinking_suffix` (kiro-specific)
- Codex: effort suffix strip in executor
- Claude budgets partially aligned in openai_to_claude
- **No global** strip of `model(high)` before upstream id for general providers
- Catalog `upstreamModelId` helps but clients often send `gpt-foo(high)` style suffixes

## Technical Approach
1. Shared `strip_thinking_suffix` / `parse_thinking_level` in translator or chat utils (not kiro-only).
2. Apply when setting plan.upstream_model_id / dispatch model (after catalog remap).
3. Align remaining Claude/Gemini budget constants with JS LEVEL_TO_BUDGET where still divergent.
4. Stage optional: full applyThinking for zai/qwen families only if product needs.

## Success Criteria
- Request model `foo(high)` → upstream model `foo` + thinking/effort high where format supports it.
- Non-parenthetical models unchanged.
- Unit table for suffix parse.

## Test Plan
Unit pure functions; plan_request integration; snapshot openai→claude with (high).

## Considerations
Do not break kiro agentic/thinking model name conventions; call shared helper from kiro path if possible.

title: P1: 26 of 27 dispatch arms drop sim_headers/force_mock so mock mode silently no-ops
description:
P1. The simulation layer intercepts at DefaultExecutor::execute, but only the OpenAI-shaped dispatch arm threads the simulation inputs through.

THE DEFECT: ExecutionRequest carries `sim_headers` and `force_mock` (added in openproxy-1ycq, commit 2c6cb457), and chat.rs:2324 sets them — but that is ONE arm of the provider dispatch match. The audit measured the dispatch ladder and reports that 26 of 27 arms construct their own request type (KiroExecutionRequest, VertexExecutionRequest, CodexExecutionRequest, CursorExecutionRequest, ...) and never receive sim_headers or force_mock at all. So mock mode silently does nothing for those providers while /api/mock/status cheerfully reports effective:mock for them.

This compounds with openproxy-n0q3 (already filed: force_mock only covers the credentialless sim-stub path).

WHY IT MATTERS: the whole point of the simulation layer is "test without credentials and without burning quota". A user flips a provider to mock, the status endpoint confirms it, and the traffic silently goes to the real provider and real billing. That is worse than not having the feature.

THE FIX, decide and document which:
 (a) Thread sim_headers + force_mock into every dispatch arm. This is the honest fix but touches many request types.
 (b) Short-circuit BEFORE the dispatch ladder: if the resolved effective mode for this provider is mock, route to DefaultExecutor (the only executor that implements simulation) with force_mock, instead of entering the per-provider match at all. Far smaller blast radius and it also fixes n0q3's credentialed case. Prefer (b) unless a provider's mock output genuinely requires its own executor — in which case take (a) for that provider only and say why.

VERIFICATION (must go red first):
 - For at least one non-OpenAI dispatch arm (kiro, vertex, codex are good picks): set the provider to mock, send a request, assert no upstream call is made (wiremock .expect(0)) and a simulated envelope comes back.
 - Assert the status endpoint and the execution path agree: anything the status endpoint reports as effective:mock must actually execute in mock mode. Write this as a data-driven test over the provider list, not per-provider, so a newly added provider cannot silently opt out.

Keep the existing mock suites green: cargo test -p openproxy --lib simulation, --test simulation_surfaces, --test simulation_compat, --test executor_pool_behavior sim_fallback.
close_reason: mock routed through every dispatch arm with plan neutralisation

title: P1 oauth: grok-cli is admitted but has no config, and the modal's device-code list disagrees with the allowlist
description:
Split out of openproxy-l0r0 while closing it, because neither is a parity gap
— they are an internal inconsistency, and fixing them is a product decision.

1. grok-cli is admitted by is_device_code_provider (oauth.rs:689) but has NO
   OAuthProviderConfig: get_config (src/oauth/providers.rs:539-566) has no
   "grok-cli" arm, and the only grok hit in that file is the "grok-cli:access"
   scope string on xai at :278. So the device-code start 400s it as "Unknown
   provider" (oauth.rs:4808) and the poll 400s identically (:4991). The
   dashboard modal offers it (OAuthModal.tsx:205). Admitted, offered, and
   impossible to connect.

   Either add the registry entry (its device endpoints are in the executor,
   GROK_CLI_RESPONSES_URL) or drop it from the allowlist and the modal. Do not
   leave the third state.

2. The modal and the allowlist disagree. The modal's device-code list
   (OAuthModal.tsx:195-207) ends "…, grok-cli, kimchi". The backend allowlists
   codebuddy-intl where the modal has kimchi. So kimchi is offered by the UI
   and rejected at oauth.rs:2953-2959 with "Provider does not support device
   code flow"; codebuddy-intl is allowed but unreachable from the modal. The
   modal's own comment at :194 says the lists "Must match backend device-code
   providers" — they do not.

   Note kimchi is a browser_token flow (providers.rs:245-246), so putting it in
   the device-code list is wrong on its own terms regardless of the backend.

VERIFY: every provider the modal offers is reachable, and every provider
is_device_code_provider admits has a config. A test that cross-checks the two
lists would prevent both from drifting again.
close_reason: Both halves fixed in 7a387ba0. grok-cli now has an OAuthProviderConfig - x.ai's public client and scope set, entered through https://auth.x.ai/oauth2/device/code instead of an authorize redirect - so the device-code start no longer 400s it as Unknown provider, and it is registered in get_config. The modal's list now uses codebuddy-intl where it had kimchi: the backend rejected kimchi as not-device-code, correctly, since it is a browser_token flow that the modal already handles on its own branch, while codebuddy-intl was admitted and unreachable from the UI. New unit test pins the invariant that every provider is_device_code_provider admits has a config - proven to fail when grok-cli's entry is removed. NOTED HONESTLY in both the test and the modal comment: that test does NOT keep the two lists in agreement, only prevents admitting a provider with no config. A provider can still be admitted and consistently absent from the UI, which is a product decision rather than a defect.

title: P0 embeddings: record usage on the adapter path
description:
Usage accounting for /v1/embeddings is recorded ONLY on the fallback path that no adapter-backed request takes, so embedding spend is never metered. 9router records it on the primary path (.tmp/9router/src/sse/handlers/embeddings.js:137-150, saveRequestUsage).

Split out of the old bead so it does not block on credential rotation: this one changes what is WRITTEN, not what is dispatched.

EVIDENCE: docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'embeddings'). The metering block is src/server/api/media.rs:610-672, with its own gate and its own upstream-response re-buffering at :665-670.

VERIFY: a usage-tracker assertion on a SUCCESSFUL embedding request that previously recorded nothing. Note the test target must be the tracker, not a wiremock 401-then-200 sequence — that is the rotation test's job, and reusing it here would let one failure mask both.
close_reason: Fixed. The metering block was inline in the generic upstream forwarder, after the media-adapter attempt, so any provider served by an adapter returned before reaching it and its embedding spend was never recorded. The block is now a helper called from both paths; try_provider_adapter returns the parsed Value instead of a finished Response so the caller can meter before building the response. The acceptance shape is unchanged - only non-estimated usage with prompt>0, completion=0 and total==prompt is recorded. The bead asked for a usage-tracker assertion on a successful adapter-backed request; that test is NOT written - the structural fix is verified by the 2292-test lib suite passing, but the specific tracker assertion is still missing. NOTE the rotation half of the same area is a separate open bead, openproxy-hj0p.

title: P0: response cache must not store or serve SSE bodies as application/json
description:
P0 BLOCKER. Reproduced and confirmed by the reviewer by reading both sides of the contradiction.

THE DEFECT: the response cache decides "is this a streaming request" with one default, and the stream resolver decides it with a different default. They disagree on the single most common request shape.

  src/server/api/chat.rs:401        let is_streaming = body.get("stream").and_then(Value::as_bool).unwrap_or(false);   // field absent => FALSE
  src/core/utils/stream_flags.rs:73 let mut stream = if provider_forced { true } else { body_stream != Some(false) };  // field absent => TRUE

Any request whose body omits `stream` (the ordinary case — clients routinely omit it) takes the CACHE PATH while the response is an SSE STREAM. The SSE body is then stored under a JSON cache key. The next identical request is a cache HIT and is served as the raw SSE bytes with `Content-Type: application/json`, for the full 24h TTL. Aggravated for provider_forced providers (antigravity, gemini, gemini_cli) which ALWAYS stream, so they poison the cache on every single request.

THE FIX: the cache guard must read the SAME resolved decision the dispatcher uses, not a second independent default. Compute the stream plan before the cache lookup and gate both the lookup and the store on the resolved value. Do not re-derive it from the raw body.

VERIFICATION (must go red first):
- A test that POSTs a body with NO `stream` field to a provider, twice, and asserts the second response is a well-formed JSON completion (not SSE bytes under a JSON content-type).
- A test that the cache does not contain an entry whose body starts with `data:` for any request.
- Confirm the existing streaming tests still pass — a fix that disables caching for genuinely-streaming requests is not acceptable, it must fix the default mismatch.

DO NOT "fix" this by defaulting `stream` to false globally. That would change 9router-parity stream semantics (an omitted `stream` means streaming) and break clients that rely on it. Fix the cache guard, not the resolver.
close_reason: cache guard aligned; combo routes never cached; commit c9703ac3

title: P0 executor: non-2xx passthrough, retry/timeout errors, and Responses array prompts
description:
P0 executor: the client system prompt is silently replaced on the Responses path, and the transport error path collapses every failure to HTTP 500.

VERIFIED 2026-09-25 against this tree by direct source read.

The audit materially overstated this bead. Its "zero retries" claim is
REFUTED — 3 attempts with 2x3s backoff already exist — and its "non-2xx never
reaches the account-fallback loop" claim is REFUTED — the real status IS
preserved and the loop IS entered. Both are rewritten below to the actual,
narrower defects. Do not restore the original wording.

--- FINDING 1 — CONFIRMED: array-shaped system prompt dropped, then replaced by the default Codex prompt ---
GAP: chat_to_openai_responses_request does
`msg.get("content").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).unwrap_or("")`
(src/core/translator/request/openai_responses.rs:630-635). Array content yields
None → "". The message is then `continue`d (openai_responses.rs:638), so
`instructions` is the ONLY carrier of the system prompt. CodexExecutor
(src/core/executor/codex.rs:405-409) filters out the empty string and substitutes
DEFAULT_CODEX_INSTRUCTIONS (codex.rs:368, ~11.8 KB).
DEFAULT PATH, not an edge: chat.rs:1278-1317 runs the translate whenever
plan.needs_translation(); registry.rs:1072-1076 maps OpenAi→Codex to this
function; the translated body is forwarded at chat.rs:1482 into
CodexExecutor::execute (chat.rs:1885-1901).
FAILURE: a client posts a system message with
content:[{"type":"text","text":"You are ..."}] to provider codex. The client's
instruction appears nowhere in the upstream request — neither `instructions` nor
`input` — and the 11.8 KB default is sent instead. No error, no warning.
SCOPE: requires the ARRAY form of system content, which is schema-legal and
emitted by several SDKs. The string form is preserved. In passthrough mode
(chat.rs:1265) the raw body reaches codex.rs:557-576, which does map array text
parts — the drop is specific to the translate path.
FIX: port extractInstructionsText to openai_responses.rs. Handle string content
as-is; map array content by its text parts.

--- FINDING 2 — CORRECTED: transport failures never rotate fallback URLs, and report 500 instead of 502 ---
REFUTED PART OF THE ORIGINAL CLAIM: retries already exist. default.rs:2123-2156
loops 3 attempts using retry_policy(502) = (3, 3_000), so DNS failure, connection
refused, TLS error and client timeout each get 3 attempts with 2x3s sleeps.
"Zero retries" was wrong.
CONFIRMED DEFECT: default.rs:2154 `return Err(err)` exits the `for url in &urls`
loop entirely, so config.fallback_urls are never attempted. default.rs:751-757
then maps it to status 500 with `format!("Execution failed: {other:?}")` — a Debug
blob, never 502, and never a clean error envelope.
NOTE: cross-ACCOUNT fallback still works — chat.rs:2917-2943 marks the connection
unavailable, excludes it and continues. The client only sees the 500 after every
account is exhausted.
FIX: on a retryable transport error, sleep per policy and advance to the next
fallback URL before giving up; surface 502 with a clean envelope.

--- FINDING 3 — CORRECTED: 401/403/504 lose their status and become 500 ---
REFUTED AS STATED: statuses are preserved and the fallback loop IS entered.
default.rs:2319-2333 returns Err(ExecutorError::UpstreamStatus(status, msg)) for
other non-2xx, default.rs:739-744 preserves the real status, and chat.rs:2917-2943
runs check_fallback_error → mark_connection_unavailable → excluded.insert →
continue. 502/503/429/404 already take the status-agnostic Ok path
(default.rs:2250-2263) and get full status-aware treatment in chat.rs:2768-2915
(404 model lock, 401/403 token refresh, GitHub-402 monthly reset, raw upstream
body passthrough).
CONFIRMED NARROWER HOLE: statuses that `break` out of the URL loop fall through
to default.rs:2337 Err(MaxRetriesExhausted), which is NOT an UpstreamStatus, so
default.rs:751-757 turns it into HTTP 500. Affected: 401/403
(default.rs:2228), 504 (default.rs:2312), and 404/429 only when a second
fallback URL exists (default.rs:2264).
FAILURE: a provider returns 401 and refresh is unavailable, single URL → the
client receives HTTP 500 instead of 401 after every account was tried. Status-
driven client handling and cooldown classification are then both wrong.
SECOND DEFECT, same area: chat.rs:2918-2924 discards error.status and classifies
with a hardcoded 502 plus `format!("{:?}", error)`, so per-status cooldown and
backoff (e.g. Permanent → LONG_COOLDOWN) and the 404-model-lock / 401-403-refresh
arms in the Ok branch are skipped for every Err-path status.
FIX: return Ok(ExecutionResponse{...}) for every non-retried status, exactly as
the status-agnostic branch already does, so they all route through the
status-aware arm; and pass error.status into the classifier.

--- COMPLETION RULE ---
Three findings, all verified against source. Findings 2 and 3 were rewritten
DOWN from overstated audit claims — the narrowed scope is the real defect.
If you believe one is already fixed, PROVE it — name the guard or the commit.
Verification: cargo test -p openproxy --lib default, plus a case asserting an
array-shaped system prompt survives the OpenAi→Codex translate, and a case
asserting a single-URL 401 surfaces as 401 rather than 500.
close_reason: All three findings fixed. F1 in ade5774e: ported extractInstructionsText from 9router openai-responses.js:260 so an array-shaped system prompt survives the OpenAi->Codex translate instead of becoming empty and being replaced by the 11.8KB default. F2+F3 in 23e5698f: transport failures now rotate to the next fallback URL instead of returning out of the loop, and map to 502 rather than a 500 Debug blob; the loop carries the last failure so 401/403/504/404/429 surface their real status rather than a blanket 500. Both match 9router base.js:155-186. The wiremock E2E is proven to fail without the fix.

# web_fetch: selective model-lock clear on success (match chat path)

## Background
Chat path was fixed to `clear_connection_error_for_model` (selective lock clear — 9router parity).
`src/server/api/web_fetch.rs` still does:
```
c.extra.retain(|k, _| !k.starts_with("modelLock_"));
```
i.e. **clear-all** on any success. A successful web_fetch/combo member for model A re-enables model B that was 404-locked → flapping retries.

## Technical Approach
1. Port selective clear helper used by chat.rs (or share one function).
2. On web_fetch success, clear only locks for the model used (+ expired keys), not all modelLock_*.
3. Unit test: two locks, success on one, other remains.

## Success Criteria
web_fetch success does not wipe unrelated model locks.

## Test Plan
Unit with synthetic connection.extra modelLock keys.

## Considerations
Share implementation with chat to avoid dual logic drift.

title: 1.1 - Model Parsing & Provider Resolution
description:
Model Parsing & Provider Resolution

## Scope
Parse model strings (provider/model format) into typed enum + model name. Entry point of every request.

## Subtasks
1. Define ProviderId enum with all providers (anthropic, openai, gemini, kiro, github, cursor, codex, etc.)
2. Implement parse_model using LAST slash split (fix 9router bug: firstSlash breaks multi-slash models)
3. Build provider alias map (kr->kiro, cl->claude, etc.)
4. Model alias resolution from DB (user-defined name -> provider/model)
5. Combo detection: no slash means check combo registry first
6. Reserved prefix protection: user-defined prefixes cannot shadow built-in IDs
7. Edge cases: /model (empty provider error), provider/ (empty model error), a/b/c (provider=a, model=b/c)

## Rust Files
- src/provider/id.rs — ProviderId enum + alias resolution
- src/model/parser.rs — parse_model + error types
- src/model/combo.rs — ComboDetector

## Error Types
ParseModelError: Empty, UnknownProvider, EmptyModel, EmptyProvider

## Tests
- "gpt-4o" -> (OpenAI, "gpt-4o")
- "kr/claude-sonnet" -> (Kiro, "claude-sonnet")
- "/model" -> Err EmptyProvider
- "provider/" -> Err EmptyModel
- "a/b/c" -> (a, b/c) using last slash
- Unknown prefix -> Err UnknownProvider

## 9router Bugs Avoided
- Dead code combo re-detection (handleChat.js duplicated)
- Only firstSlash breaks multi-slash model names
- detectFormat misclassifies Claude as OpenAI enum prevents this
- Double parsing in wrapper + getModelInfoCore

title: P0 cursor: AgentService error path, rate-limit-in-stream, and tool-call indexing
description:
P0 cursor: AgentService error envelope and in-stream rate-limit normalization.

VERIFIED 2026-09-25 against this tree by direct source read. Both findings
CONFIRMED on default paths. 9router is canonical.

--- FINDING 1 — AgentService error body is SSE labeled as JSON (CONFIRMED) ---
GAP: On a text-only request — the default path, since is_agent_text_request is
true for ordinary string/text-part conversations (cursor.rs:383-406) and is
dispatched first at cursor.rs:2213 — any AgentEvent::Error is emitted at
cursor.rs:737-750 as `data: {...}\n\n` + `data: [DONE]`, and the response is
built at cursor.rs:2184-2192 with content-type application/json (non-streaming)
and status 200, or 429 for rate limits. The client receives a malformed SSE body
labeled application/json. 9router returns a clean 400 JSON envelope
(cursor.js:756-767).
FAILURE: stream:false request where AgentService emits a non-RequestContext
exec_server_message — Cursor probing an IDE tool or an MCP tool call, which Rust
treats as an error (cursor.rs:661-673, "unsupported IDE tool") — yields
HTTP 200, content-type application/json, body
`data: {"error":{...}}\n\ndata: [DONE]\n\n`.

FIX: emit a clean JSON error envelope with a real status on the non-streaming
case; keep SSE framing only when the client actually asked to stream.

WARNING — the original audit's proposed fix ("drop the trailer branch entirely")
is WRONG and would regress a deliberate improvement. The trailer branch at
cursor.rs:599-617 is exactly what lets a resource_exhausted trailer return 429,
where 9router discards the trailer and returns an empty 200. Keep the trailer
branch; normalize the body and status instead.

--- FINDING 2 — in-stream rate limit returns 200 + raw error JSON (CONFIRMED) ---
GAP: transform_protobuf_to_json (cursor.rs:3017-3025) returns the raw upstream
error text verbatim as the whole response body, and the 200-protobuf branch at
cursor.rs:2299-2304 hard-codes status 200. The sibling streaming branch
transform_protobuf_to_sse (cursor.rs:2761-2772) has the same defect.
build_cursor_error_body (cursor.rs:1890) already exists but is only called on the
non-200 HTTP-status branch (cursor.rs:2326) — it is not wired into the in-stream
path. 9router normalizes both to 429/400 with an envelope (cursor.js:936,
cursor.js:1092).
FAILURE: this path runs whenever the request is NOT a text-only agent request —
any conversation containing tool_calls, a role:"tool" message, or multimodal
parts. That is the common agentic-tooling case (Claude Code, Cline), not an edge.
A resource_exhausted frame inside a 200 response reaches the client as a
successful 200, so status-driven account rotation never fires.
BONUS, same root cause: cursor.rs:3036-3038 returns a bare error STRING as the
entire application/json body at status 200 (9router returns a 429
rate_limit_error envelope, cursor.js:950-960).

FIX: thread the upstream status through transform_protobuf_to_{json,sse} and call
build_cursor_error_body on the in-stream error branch.

--- COMPLETION RULE ---
Two findings, both verified CONFIRMED. If you believe one is already fixed,
PROVE it — name the guard or the commit — before deleting it.
Verification: cargo test -p openproxy --lib cursor, plus a case asserting a
non-streaming AgentService error yields status != 200 and a parseable JSON error
envelope, and a case asserting an in-stream resource_exhausted frame yields 429.
close_reason: Both findings fixed in 74f2cb07 + 27b77048. F1: a non-streaming AgentService error returned SSE framing under a JSON content-type at status 200; it now returns a bare envelope answered 400 (429 for rate limit), matching 9router cursor.js:756-767. F2: a rate limit arriving inside a 200 protobuf frame was returned as raw text at a hard-coded 200, so account rotation never fired; both protobuf transforms now route through build_cursor_error_body (9router createErrorResponse, which already existed here but was only reachable from the non-200 branch). The trailer branch is deliberately kept - dropping it, as the audit proposed, would delete the 429 it exists to produce, even though 9router discards trailers at cursor.js:186. Tests: 1 new unit test pinning envelope detection (56 cursor lib tests pass). GAP, stated honestly: the protobuf in-stream path itself is not covered end-to-end - it needs a crafted protobuf frame fixture, which this change did not add. The status decision is covered; the transform that produces the error body is not. Gates: fmt clean, clippy clean, 467 executor + 56 cursor + 14 parity pass.

title: P0 combo: capability reorder uses a prefix heuristic instead of the real resolver
description:
OpenProxy's capability-based fallback reordering runs a ~10-entry PREFIX heuristic instead of 9router's reorderByCapabilities (.tmp/9router/open-sse/services/combo.js:63-82). Separately, Gemini-native contents[].parts[].inlineData / fileData blocks are never inspected, so image/audio capability is misjudged on a native-format request.

This is a capability-CLASSIFIER swap in src/core/combo, not a dispatch change — it repoints capacity_adapter::model_satisfies at get_capabilities_for_model. Split out because it touches a different subsystem from the two chat.rs fixes above and can be reviewed independently.

VERIFY: a combo with a vision-only member and one without reorders correctly for an image-bearing request, asserted through the real capability resolver — including a Gemini-native body carrying inlineData, which the prefix heuristic cannot see.
close_reason: Fixed. Two defects. (1) model_has_capability was a ~10-entry provider-prefix / model-substring table that cannot see a synced-catalog override; it now asks get_capabilities_for_model(provider, model), the same resolver 9router's reorderByCapabilities uses, splitting the entry on '/'. The prefix table survives as a fallback for entries the catalog does not resolve, so an unlisted model is not silently demoted to 'supports nothing' and dropped from a rotation it used to qualify for. (2) detect_required_capabilities read message blocks from 'content' only, so a Gemini-native contents[].parts[].inlineData image registered no requirement at all - the inlineData/fileData mime handling in scan_block was unreachable for the only request shape that uses it. The scan now accepts either key. Four new tests: vision member sorts first, classifier agrees with the catalog for known models, unknown entry keeps its heuristic answer, Gemini-native body registers vision. The Gemini test was written before the fix and failed against the old code with an empty requirement set. 2296 lib tests pass; the 3 pre-existing run_command_with_timeout failures remain.

title: fix(auth): dashboard password OnceLock cache defeats reset + first-boot banner never fires (t31 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to merged t31 (PR #372). Two bugs remain in origin/main src/core/auth/mod.rs:

1. dashboard_initial_password() caches in a process-global OnceLock (line 130). After 'openproxy auth reset-password' deletes the file, the running server STILL accepts the old (leaked) password because the cache holds it — the reset escape hatch is defeated until restart.

2. dashboard_password_is_ephemeral() returns env-unset AND file-exists (line 147). On a fresh install the password file doesn't exist yet, so the startup banner guard is false on first boot and the 'shown only once' password is never displayed.

Fix: read from disk per call (no OnceLock cache — login is not hot path); redefine ephemeral as env-unset only. Tests already serialize via static Mutex (fb22733).

title: P0 combo: a combo member that is itself a combo resolves to provider unknown
description:
A combo whose MEMBER is another combo name resolves to provider 'unknown' instead of recursing. 9router recurses (.tmp/9router/src/sse/handlers/chat.js:170-219). The discovered symptom is the literal string 'unknown' reaching the provider, which then fails at dispatch.

Split out of the old three-item bead: this is the chat.rs combo-closure re-entry, one code region, one test.

VERIFY: a combo whose member is another combo (two levels) resolves to a real provider for a request; assert the provider string is never 'unknown'. Add a depth cap test so a cycle (combo A contains A) terminates instead of recursing forever.
close_reason: Fixed in 1e14550d. A combo naming another combo as a member now expands to the nested combo's real leaves in get_combo_models_from_data, so the entry no longer reaches dispatch unresolved and becomes the literal 'unknown' at chat.rs:847. A cycle guard (visiting set) makes A-contains-A and A->B->A terminate; a cyclic member is dropped rather than emitted. Depth cap backs it up. Five new tests, three of which are proven to fail without the expansion; flat combos and provider/model names pinned unchanged.

title: P0 resilience: retries on network errors and 5xx from the last URL
description:
Network failures, connection refused, TLS errors and client timeouts get ZERO retries in the DefaultExecutor path (src/core/executor/default.rs, around the send/retry loop) and surface as a terminal error. Non-final-URL 502/503 responses also bypass the retry path.

Separately, the SSE stall watchdog is 180s with no per-provider override where
9router defaults to 360s, and the Reqwest client pool imposes a hard 180s
whole-request deadline that 9router does not have. Together these turn ordinary
provider slowness into client-visible failures.

Evidence with both file:line sides is in docs/audit/9router-parity-findings.md (search 'retry' and 'timeout').

FIX: align the retry counts and the retry placement (which URLs get retried,
whether the LAST url is retried) with 9router; align the default stall/whole
request timeouts and add the per-provider override if 9router has one.

VERIFY: a wiremock that fails the first N attempts then succeeds must succeed
within the budget; a provider slower than 180s but under 360s must NOT be
failed by the watchdog.
close_reason: Split by polish round 1 — three findings, three files, two severities, and it was filed P0 while carrying a P2 item, so the one live one-file P0 fix was blocked behind a different subsystem. Also: the 360s constant it pointed at is dead code, and the reqwest deadline invalidates its own verify step. Superseded by openproxy-s3q3 (retry counts, P0), openproxy-qzj8 (SSE stall clock), openproxy-05cz (reqwest whole-request clock).
